At the meeting, the group goes through each service area. For each, the plan records what the service is, when and how often it is given, how it is given and who gives it. Preferences, routines, cultural and language needs and goals are recorded in the resident's own terms.

The plan addresses every special care need that applies to the resident. Examples: falls (see HCS-06), pressure ulcer risk (see HCS-07), diabetes, oxygen, enteral feeding, Foley catheter, ostomy, therapeutic medication levels, mental illness and disruptive behaviors.
For a resident who smokes, the delegating nurse assesses the resident's smoking, and the plan documents any help or supervision the resident needs (see SAF-08).

For a resident who receives Community Options Waiver services, the Manager obtains the waiver plan of service from the resident's case manager. The Manager makes sure the service plan is consistent with it, reflects the resident's choices and does not restrict the resident's rights without the documentation required in SAF-04 and GOV-06.

The resident (or representative, if the resident cannot), the Manager and the delegating nurse sign and date the plan. The resident or representative receives a copy, and the plan is filed in the resident record within the 30-day deadline.

The Manager gives direct care staff access to the current plan. The delegating nurse explains new or changed plans to the staff who give the services before they begin, and the staff member signs that they have reviewed it.

The service plan is reviewed at least every 6 months, together with the assessment review. Between reviews, the delegating nurse and Manager revise the plan promptly after any significant change in condition, hospitalization, or change in the resident's preferences, and invite the resident to discuss the change.
When the plan is revised, the Manager invites the resident and, on request, the representative to discuss the revised plan, and the same signature and distribution steps are followed.

If the resident or representative disagrees with any part of the plan, the Manager documents the disagreement and the steps taken to resolve it, and tells them they may use the grievance process (see RR-02).

The Manager audits at least 3 resident records each quarter to confirm that service plans are on time, address special care needs and match the services actually delivered, and reports findings to the Quality Assurance committee (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Schedules meetings, invites participants, signs plans, ensures timeliness and distributes the plan to staff and the resident.
Prepares the plan content from the assessment, addresses special care needs and trains staff on new or changed plans.
Deliver services as written in the plan and report when the plan no longer fits the resident's needs or wishes.
Take part in plan meetings, state preferences and tell staff of changes in needs.

documentation: Signed and dated service plan in the resident record, filed within 30 calendar days of admission
Meeting invitation and attendance record
6-month review and any revisions, with dates
Smoking assessment and plan for residents who smoke
Waiver plan of service on file for waiver residents
Staff acknowledgment of plan review
Quarterly record audit results

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, delegating nurse, admissions staff and all residents
policies.purpose: To state when a resident may continue to live at [AGENCY NAME] and when a resident's needs have grown beyond what the program is licensed or able to provide, so that the resident is protected and any move is planned, timely and respectful.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] serves residents only within its licensed level of care: Level 1, 2 or 3 as stated on the license (COMAR 10.07.14.05). The program does not retain a resident who needs more than intermittent nursing care, treatment of a stage 3 or 4 pressure ulcer, ventilator services, skilled monitoring of a fluctuating acute condition, or monitoring of an uncontrollable chronic condition, or who is dangerous or at high risk in a way that cannot be managed (.23B–C). Hospice may supply services that would otherwise be excluded, as permitted by .23D. A resident who develops one of these conditions is reassessed, and the Manager either documents how the need will be met or begins discharge under ADM-06. No resident is discharged based on race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, or physical or mental disability (.23A).

definitions.definition: The level (1, low; 2, moderate; 3, high) stated on [AGENCY NAME]'s OHCQ license. A resident may be served only within that level.
Nursing care needed on an occasional or periodic basis and not on a continuous or around-the-clock basis, as determined by the delegating nurse.

A condition listed in COMAR 10.07.14.23B or C, namely more than intermittent nursing care, stage 3 or 4 ulcer treatment, ventilator services, skilled monitoring of a fluctuating acute condition, monitoring of an uncontrollable chronic condition, or a resident who is dangerous or at high risk that cannot be managed.

procedures: Staff report any new or worsening condition, behavior, wound, need for nursing care or safety concern to the Manager and delegating nurse the same day (see HCS-04).
The delegating nurse completes the reassessment required by ADM-03 and states in writing whether the resident's needs are within the licensed level and whether any .23B–C condition is present.
If the resident's needs are within the licensed level and no excluded condition is present, the Manager updates the service plan under ADM-04 and the resident stays.

If an excluded condition is present, the Manager and delegating nurse meet with the resident and, if the resident wishes, the representative and family. They discuss whether the need can be safely met, for example through the resident's practitioner, home health or hospice (see HCS-08).

If the resident is enrolled in hospice, the Manager obtains the hospice plan of care and coordinates with the hospice so that services that would otherwise be excluded are provided by hospice under .23D. The Manager documents the arrangement and the delegating nurse reviews it at each reassessment.

If the need can be met within the licensed level, the Manager documents the specific plan, who will carry it out and when it will be reviewed. The delegating nurse reassesses the resident again within 7 calendar days.

If a resident-specific level-of-care waiver is being considered, the Manager consults OHCQ before relying on it, and keeps OHCQ's response and any conditions in the resident record. Staff do not assume a waiver exists.

If a special diet ordered by the resident's practitioner is beyond the program's food service capability, the Manager tells the resident and the practitioner, and asks them to arrange another way to meet the need. If none is possible, the program begins discharge planning (see DL-01).

If the resident's needs cannot be met, the Manager begins discharge planning under ADM-06. The Manager gives written notice at least 30 calendar days before a nonemergency discharge and helps the resident find an appropriate setting.

If there is an immediate danger to the resident or others, the Manager calls 911 or arranges emergency transfer, notifies the representative and the practitioner, and follows the emergency procedures in ADM-06 and SAF-02.
The Manager keeps a written record of the decision, the reasons, the people consulted and the dates, and reports the outcome to the Quality Assurance committee.

responsibilities.duty: Determines whether the resident's needs are within the licensed level and whether a .23B–C condition is present.
Makes the retention decision with the nurse, consults OHCQ where needed, coordinates hospice and begins discharge when needs cannot be met.
Participate in decisions and tell the program about changes in needs and preferences.

documentation: Reassessment stating whether the resident is within the licensed level
Written plan for meeting the need or the decision to discharge, with reasons and dates
Hospice plan of care and coordination notes
OHCQ consultation record, if any
Notices given to the resident and representative
Practitioner communications about special diets

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, delegating nurse, business office staff, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure any discharge, transfer or relocation initiated by [AGENCY NAME] is made with proper notice, a safe plan, complete transfer information, and prompt return of money and property.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] gives the resident or representative written notice at least 30 calendar days before a nonemergency discharge. In an emergency, [AGENCY NAME] gives notice as quickly as possible and documents the reason and the abbreviated notice (COMAR 10.07.14.34B). Involuntary discharge or transfer follows the resident agreement (.34B(1)). Residents have a right to notice, procedural fairness and humane treatment (.36A(1)(aa)). A nonemergency move to another room within the facility requires 5 calendar days' notice and the resident's consent. Each discharge has a safe discharge plan that considers the resident's needs and preferences (.34C). Required records go with the resident (.34D–F). Within 30 calendar days of discharge, [AGENCY NAME] gives the final account and refunds and returns property (.34G).

definitions.definition: A discharge initiated by the facility that is not needed to protect the resident or others from immediate danger.

A summary of the resident's identifying information, diagnoses, allergies, medications, practitioner, representative and advance directives that is sent with a resident who is transferred to another facility or hospital.
A move of a resident to a different room or unit within [AGENCY NAME].

procedures: Before any discharge or relocation is proposed, the Manager reviews the reason with the delegating nurse and confirms it is permitted by the resident agreement and COMAR 10.07.14.34 (see ADM-05).

For a nonemergency discharge, the Manager gives the resident and the representative a written notice at least 30 calendar days before the discharge date. The notice states the reason, the date and the resident's right to use the grievance process (see RR-02) and to contact the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman (see RR-03). The Manager keeps a copy and the proof of delivery.
For a nonemergency relocation within the facility, the Manager gives 5 calendar days' notice and obtains the resident's consent, recorded in writing, before the move (see ADM-02).

In an emergency, the Manager notifies the resident, the representative and the practitioner as quickly as possible by phone and then in writing, and records the reason for the emergency and the length of notice given.

The Manager and delegating nurse meet with the resident and, if the resident wishes, the representative, and develop a written discharge plan. The plan considers the resident's needs and preferences, the destination, transportation, medications and continuing services.
The Manager helps the resident find an appropriate setting, contacts the receiving facility or provider, and for waiver residents notifies the waiver case manager (see GOV-06).

On the discharge date, staff send with the resident, or to the receiving facility, the emergency data sheet, current medication and treatment orders, medication administration records (MARs) and the most current Resident Assessment Tool. If the resident is going home, these are given to the resident or representative.
For an acute transfer to a hospital, staff send the emergency data sheet with copies of advance directives, the MOLST, power of attorney and guardianship papers (see RR-06 and HCS-04).
The delegating nurse prepares and releases the resident's medications according to HCS-01 and HCS-02, and the discharge is recorded on the MAR with the date and time.
Staff inventory and return the resident's property, funds and valuables, and the resident or representative signs for them (see RR-05).

The business office prepares the final statement of account. Within 30 calendar days of discharge the Manager gives the final account and refunds all amounts owed, and returns property not already returned.
If there is a suspected misuse of resident funds, the Manager cooperates with any investigation by the Attorney General and makes the records available.

The Manager completes a discharge summary in the resident record and files the discharge notice, discharge plan, transfer documents and final account in the record (see REC-01), and reports required discharges to OHCQ if required (see REC-02).
The Manager tracks every involuntary discharge and reports the count and reasons to the Quality Assurance committee.

responsibilities.duty: Decides and issues notices, develops the discharge plan, ensures transfer documents and final account are complete and on time.
Prepares the emergency data sheet and medication information and reviews the discharge plan for clinical safety.
Prepares the final account and processes refunds within 30 calendar days.
Assist with packing, inventory and transfer and ensure the resident's belongings and records go with the resident.

documentation: Written discharge or relocation notice and proof of delivery
Record of consent for any relocation within the facility
Emergency notice documentation with reasons
Discharge plan and discharge summary
Emergency data sheet, orders, MARs, Resident Assessment Tool and advance directive documents sent with the resident
Property inventory and return signature
Final statement of account and refund record

policies.title: Resident-Requested Termination and Move-Out
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, delegating nurse, business office staff and residents or representatives who choose to leave
policies.purpose: To respect a resident's choice to leave [AGENCY NAME] and to make sure the move is orderly, the financial terms of the resident agreement are followed, and the resident has the information and belongings needed to continue care safely.
policies.policy: A resident (or the representative acting for the resident) may choose to end the stay at any time. [AGENCY NAME] does not discourage, delay or penalize a resident's request to leave. The notice period and any financial terms are those stated in the resident agreement (COMAR 10.07.14.27). Within 30 calendar days of the move-out, [AGENCY NAME] gives the final statement of account, refunds amounts owed, and returns funds, property and valuables (.34G). [AGENCY NAME] gives the resident continuity-of-care information when the resident moves home or to another setting (.34D–E).

definitions.definition: A decision by the resident, or by the representative acting for the resident, to end the resident's stay at [AGENCY NAME].
The medication and treatment orders, MARs, most current Resident Assessment Tool and related information that the next provider or the resident needs to continue care.

procedures: When a resident or representative says they wish to leave, any staff member tells the Manager the same day. Staff do not argue the choice or discourage it.

The Manager meets with the resident and representative within 2 business days. The Manager listens to the reasons, asks whether any concern could be resolved, and tells the resident of the right to file a grievance (see RR-02), while making clear that the resident remains free to leave.

The Manager asks the resident to give written notice of the intended move-out date if the resident agreement requires it, and helps the resident write it if needed. The Manager explains the notice period and any financial effect stated in the resident agreement (see RR-04). If the resident cannot give the full notice period because of a health or safety need, the Manager reviews the agreement and discusses it with the resident before any charge is made.

The Manager confirms the move-out date and destination with the resident and, if the resident has a representative, with the representative. For waiver residents, the Manager notifies the waiver case manager so that services at the new setting can be arranged (see GOV-06).
The delegating nurse reviews the resident's medications and treatments and prepares what the resident will need on discharge, following HCS-01 and HCS-02 for release of medications.

Before the move, the Manager or delegating nurse reviews the information that follows the resident. This includes current medication and treatment orders, MARs and the most current Resident Assessment Tool, given to the resident or sent to the new provider with the resident's permission (see ADM-06).
The Manager helps with a safe departure plan, including transportation, a new practitioner and follow-up appointments, and the resident's questions about continuing care.
On move-out day, staff inventory the resident's property, funds and valuables with the resident and return them. The resident or representative signs for them (see RR-05).

The business office prepares the final statement of account. Within 30 calendar days of the move-out, the Manager gives the resident or representative the statement and any refund, and returns any remaining funds, property and valuables.

The Manager files the written notice, move-out documents, final statement, refund record and signed property receipt in the resident record (see REC-01) and reports the move-out to the Quality Assurance committee, noting any reasons for leaving.

responsibilities.duty: Meets with the resident, explains the agreement terms, ensures timely refunds and final account and files the records.
Prepares medication and clinical transfer information for the resident.
Prepares the final statement of account and processes refunds within 30 calendar days.
Report a resident's wish to leave to the Manager and give no pressure or discouragement.

documentation: Resident's written notice, or the Manager's note of a verbal notice
Notes of the meeting with the resident and representative
Continuity-of-care documents given to the resident or new provider
Property inventory and signed receipt
Final statement of account and refund record dated within 30 calendar days of move-out
Move-out entry in the resident record

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, delegating nurse, medication technicians, pharmacy consultant and all staff who handle medications
policies.purpose: To make sure all medications are stored securely and correctly, tracked accurately, reviewed by a pharmacist, and disposed of safely, with strict control of controlled substances to prevent loss and diversion.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] stores, tracks, reviews and disposes of medications in compliance with COMAR 10.07.14.31 and, for tasks performed by unlicensed staff, COMAR 10.27.11. Medications are kept in the original dispensed container in a secure location at the proper temperature (.31L). Schedule II–V controlled substances are counted before the close of every shift with a witness, kept double-locked, and never returned to the pharmacy (.31P). Controlled substances are destroyed on site by two qualified staff and recorded on the Division of Drug Control form (.31P(7)). A pharmacist reviews on site every 6 months the records of each resident taking 9 or more medications, including over-the-counter and PRN medications (.31I). The Manager maintains written theft and diversion procedures (.31P(5)).

definitions.definition: A drug in Schedule II, III, IV or V under state and federal law.
Stored behind two separate locks, such as a locked cabinet inside a locked room or a locked box inside a locked cabinet.
Any loss, theft or use of a medication by someone other than the person it was prescribed for.
An unlicensed staff member who has completed the Board of Nursing medication technician course and is certified, and who gives medications under the delegating nurse's supervision (COMAR 10.27.11).

procedures: The Manager designates a locked medication room or cabinet and a separate, locked refrigerator or locked compartment for refrigerated medications. Only the delegating nurse, certified medication technicians and other staff authorized by the Manager have keys or access.

The delegating nurse or a medication technician checks each new delivery against the order and the resident's name before shelving it. A medication is kept in the original dispensed container with the pharmacy label and is never transferred to another container.

Each label or record must show the resident's name, medication, reason for use, dose, frequency, route, prescriber, issue date, expiration date, refill limits and directions. If any item is missing or unclear, the nurse contacts the pharmacy or prescriber before the medication is used.
Staff keep medications at the temperature on the label. Room-temperature and refrigerator temperatures are checked and logged daily, and excursions are reported to the delegating nurse and pharmacy.
The delegating nurse removes expired, discontinued or recalled medications from the active supply every month and when a resident is discharged, and keeps them locked and separate until disposed of.
Only sealed, unopened packages or unit-dose blister packs may be returned to the pharmacy, and each return is logged with the date, medication, quantity and staff initials.

Before the close of every shift, two staff count all Schedule II–V controlled substances against the count record. The outgoing and incoming staff, or a witness, sign the count. A discrepancy is reported to the Manager and delegating nurse at once.
Controlled substances are kept double-locked at all times, and are never returned to the pharmacy.

The Manager checks whether [AGENCY NAME] must hold a Controlled Dangerous Substances registration certificate from the Office of Controlled Substances Administration, obtains it when required and keeps it on file.

To destroy controlled substances, two staff are present. One must be a licensed practitioner, pharmacist, RN, LPN, certified medication technician or licensed manager. The medication is made unusable and unrecoverable on site. Both sign the Division of Drug Control form, and the Manager sends a copy within 10 calendar days.

The Manager contracts with a licensed pharmacist for an on-site review at least every 6 months for each resident taking 9 or more medications, including OTC and PRN medications. The pharmacist's written findings go into the resident's chart, the delegating nurse follows up with the practitioner, and the Quality Assurance committee reviews the results (see GOV-04).

The Manager develops and keeps current written theft and diversion procedures covering storage, accountability, access, destruction and reporting. All staff are trained on them at orientation and yearly (see STF-03).

Staff who suspect missing or diverted medications tell the Manager immediately. The Manager investigates, files an incident report (see SAF-02), notifies the practitioner and pharmacy, and reports the loss to the authorities and OHCQ when required (see REC-02).
The Manager audits medication storage, count records and disposal records monthly and corrects any problem within 7 days.

responsibilities.duty: Controls access, maintains theft and diversion procedures, holds required registrations, arranges pharmacist reviews and sends destruction forms on time.
Oversees storage, counts, disposals and medication technicians under COMAR 10.27.11 and follows up on pharmacist findings.
Store, count, record and dispose of medications as written and report discrepancies at once.
Completes the on-site review every 6 months for residents on 9 or more medications and documents findings.

documentation: Medication labels and records showing all required information
Daily temperature logs
Shift-by-shift controlled substance count records with witness signatures
Return-to-pharmacy log
Division of Drug Control destruction forms and proof of sending within 10 calendar days
Controlled Dangerous Substances registration certificate, if required
Pharmacist on-site review reports and follow-up notes
Written theft and diversion procedures and staff training records
Incident reports for any loss or discrepancy

policies.title: Medication Administration, Medication Technicians and Self-Administration
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager, delegating nurse, medication technicians, licensed nurses and all staff who handle or assist with resident medications
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident receives medications safely, only from people who are trained and certified to give them, and that a resident who can manage his or her own medications is supported to do so safely.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] allows only licensed nurses and unlicensed staff who have completed the Maryland Board of Nursing medication technician course and hold current certification to administer medications. All administration follows COMAR 10.07.14.31, the Board of Nursing delegation rules in COMAR 10.27.11, current signed medical orders and accepted professional standards. Each resident is assessed on admission to decide whether he or she self-administers, self-administers with reminders or physical help, or needs staff administration. Administration is recorded at the time the resident takes the medication.

definitions.definition: An unlicensed staff member who completed the Board of Nursing medication technician course taught by an approved RN and holds current Board of Nursing certification.
The registered nurse under a signed agreement with the program who completed the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course and provides clinical oversight and delegation.
The resident takes his or her own medications independently, with reminders, or with physical help, as determined by the initial assessment.
The record on which each dose given, refused, held or missed is documented at the time of administration.

procedures: Only a licensed nurse or a certified medication technician may administer medications to residents. No other staff member may give a medication, and no staff member may give medications while certification is lapsed.

Before a new unlicensed staff member administers any medication, the Assisted Living Manager verifies completion of the Board of Nursing medication technician course (COMAR 10.39.04) and current certification. The manager places copies in the personnel file (see STF-05).

The manager keeps a certification tracking log. Certification renews every 2 years with 100 practice hours and a 4-hour update. The manager reminds each medication technician at least 90 days before expiration and removes the person from medication duty if renewal is not complete by the expiration date.
The delegating nurse delegates medication tasks in writing in line with COMAR 10.27.11. The delegation is limited to the medication technician's certification and demonstrated competence.

Within the admission process (ADM-01), the manager and delegating nurse assess each resident to decide whether he or she (a) self-administers, (b) self-administers with reminders or physical help, or (c) needs staff administration. The determination is recorded in the resident record.

For residents who self-administer, the delegating nurse reassesses the ability to do so at least quarterly and sooner after any significant change. The assessment is recorded and the service plan is updated if the level of help changes (ADM-04).

Staff administer medications only as written on current, signed medical orders from the resident's practitioner. Before every pass, the staff member checks the order or MAR against the pharmacy label for the right resident, medication, dose, route and time.
The medication technician records each dose on the MAR at the time the resident takes the medication. Staff never pre-chart and never document for another staff member.

If a resident refuses, a dose is held, or a medication is unavailable, the staff member documents it on the MAR and notifies the manager the same shift. The manager or delegating nurse notifies the practitioner as needed.

Staff who identify a medication error, an adverse reaction or a missed dose notify the resident's practitioner and the delegating nurse immediately, monitor the resident and complete an incident report as required by SAF-02. The manager reviews each error to find the cause and records corrective action for the QA process (GOV-04).

A resident may give medications to a spouse or domestic partner who lives in the same program only after a practitioner assessment, quarterly delegating-nurse assessments and signed orders are in place. Without all three, staff do not allow the practice.

The delegating nurse conducts an on-site medication review at least every 45 calendar days. The visit date and findings are written in the resident record and the manager acts on any recommendation within the time the nurse sets.

The manager observes medication technician practice at least [quarterly] and keeps a signed competency checklist. Any staff member who shows a practice concern is retrained or removed from medication duty until the delegating nurse confirms competence.
Storage, regimen review, pharmacist review and disposal follow HCS-01. Staff report any concern about storage, counts or labeling to the manager immediately.

responsibilities.duty: Verify certification before assignment, track renewals, keep proof in the personnel file, supervise administration and ensure orders are current.
Delegate tasks, complete self-administration assessments and quarterly reassessments, perform the 45-day on-site review and assess medication technician competence.
Give medications only as ordered, document at the time of administration, report refusals and errors immediately and maintain certification.
Carry out the manager's duties in this policy when the manager is absent.

documentation: Personnel file: medication technician course completion, Board of Nursing certification and renewal proof
Certification tracking log
Written delegation records
Self-administration assessments and quarterly reassessments in the resident record
Completed MARs
Delegating nurse 45-day review notes
Medication error incident reports and corrective action records
Practitioner assessment and signed orders for spouse or domestic partner arrangements

policies.title: Nursing Services and Delegating Nurse
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager, delegating nurse and all staff who receive delegated tasks
policies.purpose: To provide registered nurse oversight of resident care as COMAR 10.07.14.21 requires, so that delegated tasks, assessments and nursing orders are safe and carried out.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a signed agreement with a registered nurse who has completed the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course. The delegating nurse observes every resident on site at least every 45 days, is on call at all times (or a qualified alternate is), provides clinical oversight, issues nursing orders, reviews the manager's assessments and delegates tasks under the Maryland Nurse Practice Act. On-site nursing beyond these duties is provided when the delegating nurse or a practitioner orders it.

definitions.definition: The RN under a signed agreement with the program who completed the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course.
A qualified RN who meets the same requirements and covers on-call duty when the delegating nurse is unavailable.
A direction from the delegating nurse to the manager or staff about resident care that staff must carry out.
The transfer by the RN of a nursing task to a competent unlicensed staff member under Board of Nursing rules.

procedures: The governing body signs a written agreement with the delegating nurse before the program admits any resident. The agreement states the RN's duties, on-call coverage and the visit schedule, and a copy is kept in the administrative file.

Before the agreement starts, the manager obtains proof that the RN completed the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course and holds an active Maryland RN license. The manager verifies the license and keeps copies of the proof.
The governing body names an alternate delegating nurse with the same qualifications and a signed agreement. The on-call schedule is posted for staff so that an RN can be reached 24 hours a day.
The delegating nurse observes each resident on site at least every 45 days. The manager keeps a visit calendar and tells the nurse of any resident not seen by day 35.
At each visit the nurse documents the resident's condition, observations, medication review (HCS-02), skin and fall risk concerns and any nursing orders in the resident record.
The nurse reviews each assessment the manager completes using the Resident Assessment Tool (ADM-03) and documents agreement or changes. The nurse also contributes to service plans (ADM-04).
The nurse issues nursing orders in writing. The manager makes sure staff are told of each order on the same shift and carries it out or identifies an alternative with the nurse.
If the manager does not carry out a nursing order and has not identified alternatives, the delegating nurse notifies the resident's physician, OHCQ and the resident or representative.

The nurse delegates tasks only to staff who show competence. Personal care staff other than certified nursing assistants or geriatric nursing assistants show competence to the nurse before they work alone, and the nurse records the check in the personnel file.
Staff call the on-call nurse for any significant change in condition (HCS-04). The manager records each call, advice given and follow-up in the resident record.

The manager and delegating nurse meet at least every 6 months. They review resident outcomes, incidents, falls, medication errors, pharmacist findings and staffing. They keep the written minutes with the quality assurance records (GOV-04).
On-site nursing beyond the duties above is provided only when ordered by the delegating nurse or a practitioner. The manager includes any ordered nursing time in the staffing plan (STF-01).
All nursing services follow the Maryland Nurse Practice Act. Staff may not perform any task that requires a licensed nurse unless it is properly delegated or ordered.

The governing body reviews the delegating nurse arrangement at least annually as part of the quality assurance plan and replaces the nurse promptly if the agreement ends, so that there is no gap in coverage.

responsibilities.duty: Sign and renew the RN agreement, name an alternate and ensure the nurse has the resources to carry out these duties.
Visit each resident at least every 45 days, be on call, issue nursing orders, review manager assessments, delegate tasks and meet with the manager every 6 months.
Schedule visits, carry out nursing orders, call the nurse for changes in condition and keep proof of qualifications.
Carry out delegated tasks within their competence and report concerns to the manager and nurse.

documentation: Signed delegating nurse and alternate agreements
Proof of delegating nurse course completion and RN license verification
45-day visit calendar and visit notes
Nursing orders and the manager's responses
Competency records for personal care staff
Minutes of 6-month manager and nurse meetings
On-call schedule
Records of any notifications to the physician, OHCQ or resident when orders are not carried out

policies.title: Change of Condition, Practitioner Notification and Hospital Transfer
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, medication technicians, Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager and delegating nurse
policies.purpose: To make sure a change in a resident's condition is recognized, communicated quickly and acted on, and that residents who go to the hospital have the right information with them and are reassessed on return.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] documents and promptly communicates any change in a resident's condition, preferences or significant change to the resident, the resident's representative, and the practitioners and staff involved. Care notes are written at least weekly and for specified events. A full reassessment is completed within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization. An emergency data sheet accompanies every resident sent to an acute care facility, and an incident report is completed within 24 hours when an incident occurs.

definitions.definition: A major change in a resident's physical, mental or functional condition that is not expected to be short term and requires a review or revision of the service plan.
A hospital admission or emergency stay other than a planned, routine procedure.
A one-page summary that goes with a resident to an acute care facility and contains the information needed for emergency care.
A dated and signed entry in the resident record describing the resident's status, events or care given.

procedures: Any staff member who notices a new or worsening sign or symptom, a fall, a behavior change, refusal of food, fluids or medication, or any other change tells the manager or the shift lead immediately, and no later than the end of the shift.
The manager or shift lead checks on the resident and decides whether the situation is an emergency. In an emergency, staff call 911 first and then notify the manager and practitioner.

For a non-emergency change, the manager or shift lead calls the delegating nurse and the resident's practitioner the same day. Staff record the time of the call, who was reached, information given and orders received.
Staff notify the resident's representative and any person the resident has named of a significant change promptly, and record the date, time and person notified.

Staff write a care note at least weekly for every resident. They also write a note for any significant change, transfer, return from an appointment, practitioner visit, nonroutine leave and discharge.

Staff complete an incident report within 24 hours when an incident occurs, as set out in SAF-02, and notify the practitioner and delegating nurse. The manager reviews the report the same or next business day.

When a resident is sent to an acute care facility, staff prepare the emergency data sheet and send it with the resident. It lists diagnoses, current medications, allergies, diet restrictions, practitioner and representative contacts, and attaches any advance directives and the MOLST (RR-06).
Staff send the current MAR or medication list and any available insurance or Medicaid information with the resident, and the manager or delegate calls the receiving facility to give a verbal report.

The manager or delegate notifies the representative and the delegating nurse that the resident was transferred. They keep in contact with the hospital to plan the return and share any information needed for discharge planning.

Within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization, the delegating nurse and manager complete a full reassessment using the Resident Assessment Tool (ADM-03). The nurse also reassesses within 48 hours after readmission. The reassessment is signed and dated.
After the reassessment, the manager and delegating nurse update the service plan (ADM-04), invite the resident and representative to review it, and brief staff on changes before the next shift.

On return from a hospital or emergency visit, staff obtain discharge instructions and new orders, have the practitioner clarify any unclear orders and have the medication list reconciled with the pharmacy (HCS-01 and HCS-02).
If the resident's needs now exceed what the program can serve, the manager starts the process in ADM-05 and ADM-06 and does not wait for the next scheduled review.
The manager reviews change-of-condition events and hospital transfers each quarter to identify trends. The results go to the quality assurance process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Recognize and report changes immediately, write care notes and send the emergency data sheet when directed.
Ensure practitioner, nurse and representative notification, oversee reassessments and updates to the service plan, and review incident reports.
Advise on changes in condition, complete reassessments within 48 hours and review care after return from hospital.
Be informed of changes and invited to take part in updating the service plan.

documentation: Care notes (weekly and event-based)
Record of notifications to practitioner, nurse and representative
Incident reports
Emergency data sheet copy
Reassessments and updated service plans
Hospital discharge paperwork and new orders
Quarterly trend review

policies.title: Alzheimer's Special Care Unit and Dementia / Memory Care
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager, delegating nurse and all staff who work in or float to a memory care unit or serve residents with cognitive impairment
policies.purpose: To make sure any memory care service is approved by OHCQ before it opens, is staffed around the clock by trained people, and is delivered through service plans that meet the needs of residents with dementia without improper use of restraints or drugs.
policies.policy: A memory care unit at [AGENCY NAME] is an Alzheimer's Special Care Unit. The program will not operate the unit or advertise it until it has submitted the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form and received OHCQ's written approval. The unit has awake overnight staff at all times. Staff receive required cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training. Service plans address behaviors that could disrupt or harm the resident or others. The program does not use chemical or physical restraints for discipline or convenience.

definitions.definition: A designated unit or program that advertises or offers care for residents with Alzheimer's disease or other dementia and must have OHCQ approval.
The Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form submitted to OHCQ that describes the program's services, staffing and training.
Staff who are awake and on duty throughout the overnight hours; electronic monitoring does not replace them.
Required training on cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health that must be completed by hours and time frames set by regulation.

procedures: Before opening or advertising a memory care unit, the governing body submits the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form to OHCQ. The unit does not admit residents until the written approval is on file.

The manager keeps the approved Disclosure Form and the OHCQ approval letter on site. The manager updates the form and notifies OHCQ in writing if the unit's services, staffing or training change materially.

The program provides awake overnight staff in the unit every night. The staffing plan (STF-01) shows the names and schedules for the overnight staff. An electronic monitoring system is never used in place of awake staff.
The manager uses the Resident Assessment Tool (ADM-03) to decide the total staffing needed on each shift. The manager adds staff when the unit's resident needs require it.
Personal care staff in the unit complete 6 hours of cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training within 120 calendar days of hire. All other staff complete 2 hours.
Annual follow-up training is 2 hours for personal care staff and 1 hour for all other staff. The manager keeps a training tracker and certificates in each personnel file (STF-03 and STF-05).

The training covers communication, behavioral intervention, de-escalation, meaningful activities, family interaction, end-of-life care and staff stress. The manager checks each curriculum for these topics before approving it.
Before admission to the unit, the manager and delegating nurse assess whether the resident can be safely served, including wandering or exit-seeking, aggression and other risks (ADM-01 and ADM-05).

The service plan for each resident with dementia identifies behaviors likely to disrupt or harm the resident or others. It lists triggers, person-centered interventions, staff responses and the resident's preferences, life history and daily routines (ADM-04).
Staff first try non-drug approaches such as redirection, routine changes, meaningful activity and comfort measures. They record the approaches tried and the results.

The program does not use chemicals or drugs in excessive dose or duration, without indication, or with adverse consequences. The delegating nurse and pharmacist review any psychotropic order at each regimen review, and the manager asks the practitioner to reconsider an order that appears excessive.
The program does not restrain residents for discipline or convenience. Any restrictive practice is handled under SAF-04.

The program offers daily meaningful activities suited to each resident's abilities and interests (DL-02). It also follows SAF-03 for elopement prevention and response, and SAF-10 for the security of doors and the environment.
The manager invites family members and the resident's representative to take part in service plan meetings and shares information about the unit's approach to care.
The manager reviews staffing, training completion, behavior incidents, restraint use, psychotropic use and elopement events each quarter. The results go to the quality assurance process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Authorize submission of the Disclosure Form, ensure OHCQ approval before operation and fund staffing and training.
Maintain the approval, schedule awake overnight staff, assign and track training, and oversee service plans.
Assess residents for admission and behavior needs, review psychotropic orders and coach staff in non-drug approaches.
Complete required training, follow service plans and report behavior changes and safety concerns.

documentation: Submitted Disclosure Form and OHCQ written approval
Staffing plan and schedules showing awake overnight staff
Training tracker, curricula and certificates
Admission assessments and service plans addressing behaviors
Records of non-drug interventions
Psychotropic medication reviews
Quarterly unit performance review

policies.title: Falls Prevention
policies.applies_to: All staff, Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager and delegating nurse
policies.purpose: To reduce falls and fall-related injuries by identifying residents at risk, planning individualized interventions, responding promptly to falls and reporting incidents as the regulations require.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] identifies each resident's fall risk, addresses fall risk and frequent falls in the service plan with increased monitoring and intervention, and treats every fall as an incident. Incident reports are completed within 24 hours. The program notifies OHCQ within 24 hours if a resident dies from an injury incurred at the program. The manager checks daily that service plans are implemented and that ambulation devices and adaptive equipment work. Bed rails are not used without a documented determination of whether they are a restraint.

definitions.definition: An unplanned descent to the floor or other lower surface, with or without injury, whether witnessed or found.
A resident's likelihood of falling based on history, mobility, medications, cognition, vision, continence, environment and other factors.
Walkers, canes, wheelchairs, grab bars, alarms or other devices that help a resident move safely.
A device attached to a bed to prevent a resident from getting out or falling, which may be a restraint depending on its use.

procedures: At admission and each reassessment, the manager and delegating nurse assess fall risk, including fall history, gait and balance, medications, vision, continence, cognition and footwear (ADM-03).

The service plan addresses each resident's fall risk or frequent falls with specific, increased monitoring and interventions. Examples are scheduled toileting, adjusted checks, assistive devices, night lighting and supervision during transfers (ADM-04).

The manager reviews each resident's medications with the delegating nurse and pharmacist at regimen reviews for drugs that increase fall risk, and asks the practitioner to review them when needed (HCS-01 and HCS-02).

Each day the manager checks that service plan fall interventions are being carried out, and that walkers, canes, wheelchairs and other adaptive equipment are working and in good repair. The manager takes unsafe equipment out of use and arranges repair or replacement the same day.
Staff keep walkways clear, tell the manager immediately about spills, loose rugs, poor lighting or other hazards and correct them at once (SAF-10).

When a resident falls, staff stay with the resident and do not move the resident until a quick check is done for pain, injury or loss of consciousness. Staff call 911 for a suspected serious injury or head injury on anticoagulants, and otherwise call the delegating nurse for guidance.
Staff notify the practitioner, the delegating nurse and the resident's representative promptly. They record the time, who was notified and any orders received (HCS-04).
Staff complete an incident report within 24 hours of the fall, as set out in SAF-02. The report includes the location, circumstances, injuries, notifications and follow-up.
After every fall, the manager and delegating nurse review the cause and update the service plan within [two] business days. They add the post-fall monitoring that the nurse orders.
A fall with a significant change in condition or a nonroutine hospitalization triggers a full reassessment within 48 hours (HCS-04).
If a resident dies from an injury incurred at the program, including a fall, the manager notifies OHCQ within 24 hours and follows SAF-02, HCS-09 and REC-02.

Before any bed rail is installed or requested, the manager and delegating nurse determine whether it functions as a restraint for that resident. They document the determination in the record and apply SAF-04 if it is a restraint.
If the program has 17 or more beds, the manager makes sure assist rails are installed on both sides of resident corridors and checks them in the monthly safety inspection (SAF-10).
The manager tracks falls monthly by resident, time, location and cause, and reports trends to the quality assurance committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Check daily that fall interventions and equipment are in place, review every fall, and ensure reporting and service plan updates.
Assess fall risk, review medications and post-fall status, and advise on interventions.
Follow fall interventions, respond to falls and report hazards and equipment problems.
Repair equipment and correct environmental hazards promptly.

documentation: Fall risk assessments
Service plans with fall interventions
Daily manager check record
Equipment inspection and repair log
Incident reports and post-fall follow-up notes
Bed rail restraint determinations
Monthly fall tracking log and QA review

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Prevention
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager and delegating nurse
policies.purpose: To prevent pressure injuries and other skin breakdown, detect skin changes early and make sure the program does not serve residents whose wound care needs exceed what a Maryland assisted living program may provide.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] addresses pressure ulcer risk, prevention and treatment in each resident's service plan. The program does not admit a person who needs treatment for stage 3 or stage 4 skin ulcers, except under a hospice plan of care. Weights are kept monthly or as the practitioner orders. Skin changes are reported to the delegating nurse, and a significant change triggers a full reassessment within 48 hours.

definitions.definition: Localized damage to the skin or underlying tissue, usually over a bony prominence, caused by pressure or pressure with shear.
A full-thickness skin loss (stage 3) or full-thickness skin and tissue loss with exposed muscle or bone (stage 4).
A visual look at a resident's skin, with attention to bony areas and areas under devices or clothing, performed during personal care.
A major change in condition that is not expected to be short term and requires reassessment.

procedures: At pre-admission screening, the manager and delegating nurse review the applicant's skin condition. The program does not admit a person who requires treatment of stage 3 or 4 skin ulcers, except under a hospice plan of care (ADM-01 and HCS-08).
At admission, the delegating nurse or manager documents a baseline skin assessment, including any existing wounds, in the resident record, and records the risk for skin breakdown (ADM-03).

The service plan addresses each resident's pressure ulcer risk, prevention and treatment. It lists repositioning needs, pressure-relieving devices, nutrition and hydration, continence care, skin care products and who does what (ADM-04).

Staff look at the resident's skin during bathing, dressing and incontinence care. They report any redness that does not fade, blister, open area, bruise, swelling, warmth or pain to the manager or shift lead before the end of the shift.

The manager or shift lead tells the delegating nurse of any skin change on the same day. The nurse sees the resident on site or gives direction by phone, and records the assessment and any nursing orders.
The nurse or manager notifies the practitioner and the resident's representative of any new skin breakdown and records the notification and any orders (HCS-04).

Staff reposition residents who cannot change position on their own at the interval in the service plan. They use pressure-relieving cushions or mattresses as ordered and keep the heels and bony areas free of pressure.
Staff follow the diet and fluid plan in the service plan and report poor intake. The program works with dietary staff on any therapeutic diet (DL-01).
Staff weigh each resident monthly, or as the practitioner orders, and record the weight in the resident record. They report a weight loss to the delegating nurse.
Only staff who are licensed or properly delegated by the nurse perform wound or skin treatments. Staff carry out treatments only as written in practitioner or nursing orders.

If a resident develops a wound that progresses to stage 3 or 4, or otherwise needs care beyond the program's limits, the manager and nurse start the review in ADM-05. They arrange appropriate care or relocation under ADM-06, unless the resident is under a hospice plan of care.
A significant change in skin condition, or a return from a nonroutine hospitalization, triggers a full reassessment within 48 hours, and the service plan is updated (ADM-03 and ADM-04).
The manager tracks the number and stage of pressure injuries, and presents the data to the quality assurance process each quarter (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Check skin during care, reposition as planned, and report skin changes the same shift.
Assess skin changes, issue nursing orders, direct treatments and judge whether needs exceed program limits.
Ensure the service plan is implemented, weights are taken and recorded, and admission and retention limits are applied.
Evaluate wounds and issue treatment orders when notified.

documentation: Pre-admission and admission skin assessments
Service plans addressing pressure ulcer risk
Skin change reports and nurse assessments
Monthly weight record
Practitioner and nursing treatment orders
Notification records
Reassessments after significant change
Quarterly pressure injury tracking

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
policies.applies_to: All residents receiving hospice, home health or other outside clinical services; Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager, delegating nurse, direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure residents can receive hospice, home health and other outside services in the facility, that responsibilities are divided clearly between the facility and each outside provider, and that care stays safe, coordinated and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] helps residents get home health, hospice, rehabilitation, skilled nursing and other services identified in the Resident Assessment Tool or requested by the resident. When a resident is under a licensed general hospice program in the facility, the hospice and the assisted living program each comply with their own regulations: COMAR 10.07.14, COMAR 10.07.21 and applicable federal rules (COMAR 10.07.14.38H). The admission and retention exclusions in COMAR 10.07.14.23B and C do not apply to a hospice resident when the hospice plan of care delivers the services that would otherwise be excluded (COMAR 10.07.14.23D). The facility does not take over any service the hospice or home health agency is responsible for providing. Hospice orders, the MOLST and care notes are kept in the resident record.

definitions.definition: A licensed general hospice care program, regulated under COMAR 10.07.21, that provides palliative and end-of-life care to a resident in the facility.
A licensed outside agency that provides skilled nursing, therapy or aide services to a resident in the facility under a practitioner's order.

The written plan developed by the hospice, with the resident and representative, that lists the services the hospice will provide, including any services that would otherwise be excluded under COMAR 10.07.14.23B and C.
The assessment instrument required by COMAR 10.07.14.02 and used to determine the resident's level of care and service needs.
The registered nurse who delegates nursing tasks to unlicensed staff and oversees resident care under COMAR 10.07.14.02.

procedures: When the Resident Assessment Tool, a practitioner, the resident or the representative identifies a need for home health, hospice, rehabilitation or skilled nursing services, the Assisted Living Manager (or designee) arranges a referral within [1] business day and records it in the resident record.
The resident or representative chooses the outside provider. Staff give a list of available licensed providers and do not steer residents to a provider for the facility's convenience.
Before an outside provider starts, the Manager obtains the practitioner's order, the provider's name and 24-hour contact number, and the start date, and files them in the resident record.
For a hospice referral, the Manager confirms that the hospice is licensed by OHCQ as a general hospice care program and obtains a copy of the hospice agency's contact list and on-call instructions.

The Manager and the hospice sign a written coordination agreement, or document an equivalent written understanding, that states who provides each service, who responds to after-hours needs, and who is notified of a change in condition. It is kept in the resident record.

The Manager obtains the hospice plan of care and compares it with the service plan. If the hospice plan delivers a service that would otherwise be excluded under COMAR 10.07.14.23B or C (for example, more than intermittent nursing care or treatment of a stage 3 or 4 ulcer), the Manager documents that the hospice exception applies and that the hospice is providing that service.

If the hospice plan does not deliver an excluded service, the Manager does not rely on the hospice exception. The Manager then reviews retention under ADM-05 and, if needed, relocation or discharge under ADM-06.

Within 48 hours after the start of hospice or home health services, which is a significant change, the delegating nurse completes a full assessment. The service plan is updated to reflect the resident's wishes and the roles of the facility and the outside provider (COMAR 10.07.14.28).

The service plan meeting includes the resident, the representative, the hospice or home health case manager when possible, and the delegating nurse. The Manager invites them and records the invitation and attendance.

Staff file hospice and home health orders, the MOLST, advance directives, visit notes and medication lists in the resident record. Staff transcribe or follow each new order the same day under HCS-01 and HCS-02.

Staff follow the medication rules in HCS-01 and HCS-02 for hospice medications, including comfort kits. Controlled substances are counted each shift, double-locked and destroyed as required. Staff do not give a hospice medication unless the medication technician or nurse has the order and the instructions.

Staff report any change in condition to the hospice or home health agency, the practitioner, the delegating nurse and the representative as required by HCS-04. Staff call the hospice number first for a hospice resident unless the situation is an emergency requiring 911.

The Manager does not allow a hospice resident to be sent to a hospital unless the resident's wishes, the MOLST and the hospice have been checked, except where 911 is needed in an emergency and the MOLST allows it.

Facility staff keep providing personal care, meals, activities, housekeeping and supervision as listed in the service plan. Staff may be trained by the hospice or home health nurse for resident-specific tasks, and that training is documented along with the delegating nurse's delegation under HCS-03.
If the resident under hospice is restrained or uses bed rails, the facility follows SAF-04 and the hospice follows its own chapter (COMAR 10.07.14.38H).

When hospice or home health services end, the Manager records the date and reason, the delegating nurse reassesses the resident, and the Manager decides whether the resident can stay in the facility under ADM-05.
Staff handle a resident's death under hospice in accordance with HCS-09.

responsibilities.duty: Arrange referrals, sign coordination agreements, confirm licensure of outside providers, apply the hospice exception correctly, and keep documentation complete.
Assess residents after a significant change, update the service plan, coordinate with outside nurses, train staff on resident-specific tasks and review hospice-related medication handling.

responsibilities.role: Medication technicians and direct care staff
responsibilities.duty: Follow current orders, provide the personal care in the service plan, notify the nurse and the hospice or agency of any change, and document in care notes.
Provide the services in its plan of care, give the facility its orders, visit notes and after-hours contacts, and comply with its own licensing chapter.

documentation: Referral record and practitioner order for each outside service
Written coordination agreement or documented understanding with the hospice or home health agency
Hospice plan of care and documentation that the COMAR 10.07.14.23D exception applies
Significant change assessment and updated service plan
Hospice and home health orders, MOLST and visit notes filed in the resident record
Care notes of communications with the hospice, agency, practitioner and representative

policies.title: Death of a Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff; Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager, delegating nurse
policies.purpose: To make sure that a resident's death is handled with dignity and in line with the resident's wishes, that required notifications and reports are made on time, and that the resident's record, belongings and money are handled properly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] treats every resident death with respect for the resident, the family and other residents. Staff follow the MOLST and advance directives, notify the practitioner, the representative and family without delay, and document the death in the resident record. The facility completes an incident report within 24 hours and notifies OHCQ within 24 hours when a death results from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program (COMAR 10.07.14.33). Within 30 calendar days the facility gives the final statement and any refund to the resident's agent and returns the resident's property and valuables (COMAR 10.07.14.34). The record is kept 5 years (COMAR 10.07.14.29).

definitions.definition: The written report required by COMAR 10.07.14.33, completed within 24 hours of the facility's knowledge of the event.
Maryland Medical Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment, the medical order form that states the resident's resuscitation and treatment preferences.
The resident's representative, personal representative, executor or other person legally authorized to receive the final statement, refund and property.

procedures: When staff find a resident who may have died or is in cardiac or respiratory arrest, the staff member checks the MOLST and advance directive kept in the resident record or at the location listed in the emergency data sheet.

If the MOLST or an advance directive calls for resuscitation, staff begin CPR and call 911 at once. If the MOLST or advance directive declines resuscitation, staff do not start CPR and follow the instructions in the MOLST, the practitioner's orders and, for a hospice resident, the hospice's procedure.

Staff immediately notify the Assisted Living Manager (or Alternate Manager) and the delegating nurse. The Manager calls 911 or the hospice, as appropriate, so that the death is pronounced and the death certificate process is started under Maryland law.

If the death is unexpected, or the circumstances suggest injury, abuse, neglect, a medication error, a fall or a fire, staff call 911 and law enforcement, do not disturb the area or the resident's belongings beyond what is needed for care, and notify the Manager at once.
The Manager notifies the resident's practitioner and the resident's representative and listed emergency contacts as soon as possible, and records the date, time and name of each person notified.

Within 24 hours of learning of the death, the Manager or designee completes an incident report under SAF-02 whenever the death resulted from, or may have resulted from, an incident, and keeps it on the premises.

If the death resulted from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program, the Manager notifies OHCQ within 24 hours at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005 and documents the call.
If abuse or neglect is suspected, the Manager also reports within 24 hours to every party required under SAF-01 and protects other residents while the matter is investigated.

The delegating nurse or a designee writes a care note that records the death, the location, the manner or circumstances, the time found, the time pronounced, the person who pronounced the death, and the people notified.

Staff preserve the resident's privacy, close the door, and arrange for the resident's body to be released to the funeral home chosen by the family or the resident's documented wishes. The Manager records the funeral home and the time of release.
Staff tell other residents about the death in a gentle way, offering support as needed, while keeping the deceased resident's information confidential under RR-07.

The Manager and one other staff member inventory the resident's room, belongings, valuables and any personal funds held by the facility, using the facility's personal property inventory and RR-05. Both sign the inventory.
The facility releases property and valuables only to the resident's agent after verifying identity and authority, obtains a signed receipt, and records the date.

If no family, representative or agent can be found or none claims the deceased resident, the Manager does not make burial arrangements alone. The Manager contacts OHCQ, the local department of social services and the Ombudsman, follows the process and approvals required by OHCQ regulations and Maryland law, and documents each step.

Within 30 calendar days of the death, the Manager prepares the final statement, calculates any refund of fees or deposits under RR-04, and gives the statement and refund to the resident's agent. The Manager keeps a copy and proof of delivery.

The delegating nurse and the Manager check that medications of the deceased resident are removed from active use, held or destroyed according to HCS-01, and that any controlled substances are counted and destroyed with a witness.
The Manager closes the resident's record, files the final statement, the property inventory and receipts, and keeps the record for 5 years after the date of death.
The Manager reviews the death at the next quality assurance meeting under GOV-04 to find any needed changes to care or procedures.

responsibilities.duty: Direct the response, make notifications and reports, complete the final statement, refund and property return within 30 calendar days, and keep documentation.
Review the MOLST and orders, document the death in a care note, support staff, and oversee the disposition of medications.
Check the MOLST, call 911 or the Manager as directed, preserve privacy and dignity, and report promptly.
Carry out these duties whenever the Manager is not available.

documentation: Care note recording the death, location, manner and notifications
MOLST and advance directives
Incident report completed within 24 hours when applicable
Record of the OHCQ notification within 24 hours when applicable
Property and valuables inventory, release receipts and funeral home release record
Final statement, refund calculation and proof of delivery
Medication disposition record
Closed resident record retained 5 years

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, volunteers, contractors, Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager and governing body
policies.purpose: To prohibit abuse, neglect and financial exploitation of residents, to prevent them through hiring and training, and to make sure every suspected case is reported within 24 hours, investigated and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] prohibits abuse, neglect and financial exploitation of any resident by any person. This is the written prohibition policy required by COMAR 10.07.14.37A. The facility does not knowingly employ anyone with a criminal conviction or history that indicates behavior potentially harmful to residents (COMAR 10.07.14.37B), and completes the criminal history records check required by Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901 before employment. Any person who suspects or learns of abuse, neglect or exploitation reports it at once to the Assisted Living Manager and the report is made within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services, and the Manager (COMAR 10.07.14.37C). A person who reports in good faith is immune from civil liability under Md. Code, Health-General §19-347(g). The facility does not retaliate against reporters or residents.

definitions.definition: Any willful act or omission that causes physical harm, pain, mental anguish or sexual contact without consent, including verbal, emotional and physical abuse, and any form of involuntary seclusion or improper restraint.
Failure to provide the care, supervision, food, medication, hygiene or protection a resident needs, whether or not intended.
Improper use of a resident's money, property or assets, including theft, coercion, undue influence, misuse of a power of attorney, and charging for services not provided.
The local long-term care Ombudsman program or area agency on aging that receives reports under COMAR 10.07.14.37C.
Adult Protective Services in the local Department of Human Services.

procedures: Before any person is hired, the Manager verifies the age and qualifications required by COMAR 10.07.14.19 and obtains the criminal history records check (Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901) within 30 calendar days before employment. The Manager reviews the result under STF-02 and does not knowingly employ anyone whose history indicates behavior potentially harmful to residents.

At orientation, and annually in the required training under STF-03, every employee, relief staff member and volunteer receives and signs this policy and is trained to recognize signs of abuse, neglect and exploitation, to report, and to use de-escalation and dignity-preserving care.

The Manager posts reporting signs in employee and public areas that give the numbers for OHCQ ((410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005), the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, local APS and local law enforcement. The Manager checks monthly that the signs remain posted and legible.

Staff protect residents at once. Any person who sees or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation stops the harm if safe to do so, gets medical care if needed, calls 911 if there is immediate danger, and makes sure the resident is safe.

The staff member who sees or suspects the event reports to the Assisted Living Manager at once. If the Manager is suspected, the staff member reports to the Alternate Manager, the governing body representative [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or the agencies listed below.

Within 24 hours of the suspicion or knowledge, the Manager (or the staff member if the Manager is suspected) reports orally or in writing to: (a) law enforcement; (b) OHCQ; (c) the Ombudsman or area agency on aging; (d) the local DHS/APS; and (e) the Manager. The Manager records the date, time, person contacted and any reference number.

The Manager treats any report not made within 3 days as a violation that can result in a penalty of up to $1,000, and corrects any delay at once. The Manager reviews every case for timeliness at the next quality assurance meeting.

If a licensed or certified individual (for example, a nurse or certified medication technician) fails to report, the Manager considers referral to the licensing or certifying board as permitted by COMAR 10.07.14.37C.

The Manager notifies the resident's representative and practitioner, unless the representative is suspected, and documents the notification. The Manager also records the event under SAF-02 within 24 hours.

The Manager protects residents during the investigation: separating the accused from contact with the resident and any other resident at risk, reassigning or suspending the accused employee pending the outcome, offering medical and emotional support, and arranging a safe placement if needed.

The Manager starts an investigation immediately. The investigation includes interviews with the resident, witnesses and the accused, review of schedules, records and any video, physical evidence, and a written summary with findings and corrective action. The Manager completes the investigation within [5] business days unless law enforcement or OHCQ directs otherwise.
The facility keeps all investigation documentation on site and available to OHCQ.

The Manager sends the investigation report to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging and APS. When the facts indicate a crime or Medicaid fraud, the Manager supports referral to the State's attorney or the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit.

If an allegation is substantiated, the Manager imposes corrective action up to and including termination, notifies licensing boards where required, and reviews the facility's hiring, training and supervision practices.

No person is penalized for a good-faith report. Retaliation against a reporter or resident is itself a violation of this policy and leads to discipline. Staff are told that a good-faith reporter has civil immunity under Md. Code, Health-General §19-347(g).

The Manager prevents financial exploitation by following RR-05: staff may not borrow from, accept gifts from, serve as agent or witness for, or hold funds of a resident except as allowed by RR-05 and STF-06.
The governing body reviews a summary of all reports and outcomes under GOV-04 at least [quarterly].

responsibilities.duty: Prevent harm, report suspicions to the Manager at once, cooperate in investigations and never retaliate.
Ensure 24-hour reports to all required parties, protect residents, investigate, keep documentation on site and post signs.
Act for the Manager in the Manager's absence or when the Manager is the subject of a report.
Receive reports about the Manager, review outcomes, and ensure resources for training and prevention.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy and training records
Criminal history records check results and hiring decisions
Record of each 24-hour report with date, time, agency and person contacted
Written investigation file with interviews, findings and corrective actions
Investigation reports sent to law enforcement, OHCQ, Ombudsman/AAA and APS
Incident report under SAF-02
Photo or log of posted reporting signs and monthly checks

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
policies.applies_to: All staff; Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager, delegating nurse
policies.purpose: To make sure every incident involving a resident is promptly reported, documented, followed up and used to prevent recurrence, and that required notifications are made.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires staff to complete an incident report within 24 hours of learning of any incident, using the definition of "incident" in COMAR 10.07.14.02B (COMAR 10.07.14.33A). Each report records the time, date and place, the individuals present, a complete description, the staff response, notifications made, and follow-up and prevention steps (COMAR 10.07.14.33C). Reports are kept on the premises and are available to OHCQ and designated agencies (COMAR 10.07.14.33B). The facility notifies OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death resulting from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program (COMAR 10.07.14.33D).

definitions.definition: An event as defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02B. The facility applies the definition broadly and treats as an incident any accident, injury, fall, elopement or wandering, medication error, allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation, death, or other event that affects or could affect a resident's health, safety or welfare.
The written record of an incident completed within 24 hours of knowledge.
The registered nurse who delegates tasks and reviews resident care under COMAR 10.07.14.02.

procedures: Any staff member who sees, finds or hears about an incident first makes sure the resident is safe, gets first aid or calls 911 if needed, and tells the Assisted Living Manager or the person in charge at once.
The person in charge notifies the delegating nurse of any injury, fall, medication error or change in condition so that the nurse can assess the resident or direct care.

The staff member who witnessed or discovered the incident completes the incident report before the end of the shift, and in all cases within 24 hours of learning of the incident. The report is not delayed for the investigation.
The report states the time, date and place; the names of the resident and each person present; a complete, factual description of what happened (not opinions); and the staff response and care given.

The report records notification of the resident or representative, the resident's practitioner, the delegating nurse, and, when appropriate, OHCQ, law enforcement and other authorities, with the date, time and person contacted.
