The Manager notifies the resident's representative and practitioner promptly for any injury, transfer to a hospital, medication error, or event with possible effect on health. The notification is recorded in the incident report and in a care note.
If abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, the Manager also follows SAF-01 and makes the 24-hour reports required there.
If the incident is an elopement or missing resident, the Manager follows SAF-03. If it is a fall, the Manager follows HCS-06. If it involves a medication error, the Manager follows HCS-01 and HCS-02.

If a resident dies as a result of abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program, the Manager notifies OHCQ within 24 hours at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005 and records the call.

The Manager reviews every incident report within [1] business day, signs and dates it, and records the follow-up and prevention steps taken, such as service plan changes, staff retraining, equipment repair or environmental changes.
If the incident indicates a significant change in the resident's condition, the delegating nurse reassesses the resident and the service plan is updated under ADM-03 and ADM-04.

The Manager files the original incident report in the facility's incident file on the premises and places a note in the resident record referring to the event. Reports are kept in a way that allows OHCQ and designated agencies to inspect them.
The Manager reviews incidents each month to identify trends by resident, time, place and staff, and reports the results to the quality assurance committee under GOV-04.
The Manager reviews this policy with staff at orientation and annually, including how to complete the report accurately and on time.

responsibilities.role: Staff member who knows of the incident
responsibilities.duty: Protect the resident, report to the Manager and complete the incident report within 24 hours.
Make notifications, review and sign reports, notify OHCQ when a death falls under COMAR 10.07.14.33D, ensure follow-up and keep reports on site.
Assess residents after incidents, advise on notifications, and recommend care and service plan changes.

documentation: Completed, dated incident report with all required content
Notification log or notes for representative, practitioner, delegating nurse, OHCQ and law enforcement
Follow-up and prevention steps and Manager review signature
Care note and service plan update when applicable
Monthly incident trend review in quality assurance minutes

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff, all shifts; Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager, delegating nurse
policies.purpose: To prevent residents from leaving the facility unsafely or without supervision, to find a missing resident quickly, and to report and learn from every elopement.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] identifies residents at risk of wandering or elopement, protects them through supervision, staffing and environmental safeguards, and responds immediately when a resident is missing. Staff are present whenever a resident is in the building, and awake overnight staff are provided when the Resident Assessment Tool requires it (COMAR 10.07.14.14). An electronic monitoring waiver is not available on an Alzheimer's special care unit. The facility completes an incident report within 24 hours of any elopement (COMAR 10.07.14.33A) and notifies OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death from wandering or elopement (COMAR 10.07.14.33D). The facility uses its emergency tracking system and resident identification required by COMAR 10.07.14.47C.

definitions.definition: A resident leaving the facility or its grounds without staff knowledge, without needed supervision, or without the knowledge of the resident's representative when supervision is required.
Aimless or purposeful movement by a resident, often from cognitive impairment, that puts the resident at risk of leaving a safe area.
The assessment required by COMAR 10.07.14.02 that determines care needs, including whether awake overnight staff are required.

procedures: Before or at admission, the delegating nurse and Manager screen each resident for wandering and elopement risk using the pre-admission screening under ADM-01 and the Resident Assessment Tool. They record the result in the resident record.

For each resident at risk, the service plan states the supervision level, triggers, interventions such as redirection, meaningful activity and toileting schedules, and who will carry them out (see ADM-04).
The Manager reassesses a resident who wanders after any elopement, change in condition or wandering behavior, and updates the service plan.

The Manager keeps a current photograph, description, identifying marks, diagnoses, medications and an emergency contact for each at-risk resident in the emergency tracking system and medical fact sheet, and updates these at least [quarterly] and after any change.

Each at-risk resident wears or carries the identification the facility has chosen (for example, a bracelet or ID card) that has the facility's name and phone number, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.47C.

The Manager sets the staffing plan under STF-01 so that staff are present whenever a resident is in the building and so that awake overnight staff are on duty whenever the Resident Assessment Tool requires it. The facility does not use an electronic monitoring waiver for an Alzheimer's special care unit.

The Manager maintains the facility's door controls, alarms, fencing and other security measures in line with the security requirements of COMAR 10.07.14 and SAF-10, tests alarms at least [weekly], and fixes any failure the same day, with staff posted at the door until the repair is complete.
Staff count residents at the start of each shift, at each meal and activity, and before and after outings, and record the count. Any resident who cannot be located is treated as missing.

When a resident is missing, the staff member who notices immediately shouts or radios a missing-resident alert, announces the resident's name and description, and notifies the Manager or person in charge.

The person in charge assigns staff to search the building, grounds and nearby areas using a checklist (bathrooms, closets, stairwells, vehicles, nearby streets and water), starting with the places where the resident has been found before, while at least one staff member stays with the other residents.

If the resident is not found within [10] minutes of the alert, or immediately if the resident is high-risk, the weather is extreme, or the resident is medically fragile, the person in charge calls 911, gives the description and photograph, and calls the representative and practitioner.

The person in charge notifies the Manager, delegating nurse and [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and continues the search until the resident is found. Staff do not stop searching because law enforcement has been called.

When the resident is found, staff assess the resident for injury and call 911 or the practitioner if needed. The delegating nurse completes an assessment and the resident is returned safely. The representative and practitioner are notified.
Within 24 hours of the elopement, the staff member in charge completes an incident report under SAF-02, and the Manager reviews it and records the cause and the prevention steps.
If a resident dies from wandering or elopement, the Manager notifies OHCQ within 24 hours at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005 and follows HCS-09.

After every elopement, the delegating nurse and Manager reassess the resident's risk, change the service plan, add supervision, and decide whether the facility can continue to meet the resident's needs under ADM-05.
The Manager trains all staff on this policy at orientation and annually and runs a missing-resident drill at least [twice a year], including on the night shift, and records the results.

responsibilities.duty: Supervise at-risk residents, count residents, sound the alert and search at once.

responsibilities.role: Person in charge on the shift
responsibilities.duty: Direct the search, call 911, notify the Manager, representative and practitioner.
Maintain security, staffing and the tracking system, complete the incident review, notify OHCQ when required and run drills.
Assess risk, post-event condition and service plan changes.

documentation: Wandering and elopement risk assessment and service plan interventions
Emergency tracking system, photographs and medical fact sheets
Resident counts and door alarm test logs
Missing-resident search record and 911 call record
Incident report within 24 hours and OHCQ notification when required
Reassessment and updated service plan
Missing-resident drill records

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
policies.applies_to: All staff; Assisted Living Manager, delegating nurse, medication technicians
policies.purpose: To protect residents' right to be free from involuntary seclusion and improper restraint, to allow restraint only when a physician orders it for a specific symptom or condition, and to keep any resident who is restrained safe and informed.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not use restraints for discipline or convenience. Residents have the right to be free from involuntary seclusion and from restraints used in violation of COMAR 10.07.14 (COMAR 10.07.14.36A(1)(i) and .38A). A physical restraint is used only with a physician's order for a specific symptom or condition (COMAR 10.07.14.38D). The order states the purpose, type and duration, is time-specific, and may not be a PRN order (COMAR 10.07.14.38E). A restrained resident is repositioned and offered toileting at least every 2 hours, and the order is renewed at least every 7 calendar days. Chemical restraint is prohibited. Where a resident is under hospice care, the hospice and the facility each follow their own chapter (COMAR 10.07.14.38H). For residents funded through the Community Options Waiver, any restriction of a resident's rights is also subject to the home and community-based settings requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c) and GOV-06.

definitions.definition: A physical, mechanical or chemical means that restricts a resident's freedom of movement or normal access to the body, and that the resident cannot remove easily.

A device as defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02B that is not a restraint (COMAR 10.07.14.38B), such as a device that protects the resident without restricting movement or that the resident can remove or use voluntarily.
A drug used to control behavior or restrict movement that is given in excessive dose, for excessive duration, without adequate indication or despite adverse effects.
Separating a resident from others against the resident's will or confining the resident to a room or area.
An order given only "as needed." PRN restraint orders are prohibited.

procedures: Staff use the least restrictive approach first. Before any restraint is considered, the delegating nurse and Manager review the cause of the resident's behavior or condition and try alternatives such as redirection, activities, pain control, toileting, adjusting the environment, supervision or equipment such as a low bed.

No staff member may apply a restraint, lock a resident in a room or seclude a resident for discipline, convenience or staffing reasons. A staff member who is directed to do so reports it to the Manager and, if necessary, under SAF-01.

A physical restraint is applied only after the resident's physician has examined the resident and issued a written order that treats a symptom or condition. The order must state the purpose, type of restraint and duration.
The Manager does not accept a PRN or open-ended restraint order and asks the physician for a time-specific order. The Manager records the request.

The delegating nurse (or a registered nurse designated by the facility) trains each staff member who will use the ordered restraint in the correct use, safety checks and release, and records the training and the staff member's name and date.

Before the first use, the Manager informs the resident and the representative of the order, the reason, the type and the expected duration, and records the discussion and consent. The Manager notifies the family or representative each time a restraint is used and records it.

Staff check on the restrained resident at least every [30] minutes, reposition the resident, and offer toileting at least every 2 hours. Staff record each check, repositioning and toileting offer, and the resident's skin, circulation and comfort.
The physician's order is renewed at least every 7 calendar days. The Manager tracks the renewal date, and no restraint continues after the order expires.

The delegating nurse reassesses the resident at each renewal for the need for the restraint, injury, skin condition, function, and a plan to reduce or end it, and updates the service plan under ADM-04.

The Manager treats a bed rail as a possible restraint and the delegating nurse determines for each resident whether it restricts the resident's movement. The determination is documented per resident. If it is a restraint, this policy applies, including a physician's order.

Staff use a device that meets the definition of a protective device under COMAR 10.07.14.02B only after the delegating nurse documents that it is not a restraint and the resident has been offered alternatives.

The facility prohibits chemical restraint. The delegating nurse reviews each resident's medications during the medication regimen review under HCS-01 and HCS-02 to check for drugs given in excessive dose or duration, without adequate indication, or despite adverse effects, and asks the prescriber to review any concern.

For a Community Options Waiver resident, the Manager may not use a restriction without the person-centered service plan documentation required by 42 CFR 441.301(c), including the assessed need, less intrusive methods tried, informed consent and periodic review.
If a resident is under hospice care, the delegating nurse coordinates with the hospice so that each provider follows its own chapter and the orders are consistent.

The Manager discontinues the restraint as soon as the condition no longer requires it, and records the date and the resident's response. Emergency use of force to prevent immediate harm is limited to the minimum time and treated as an incident under SAF-02.
The Manager reviews all restraint use and bed rail determinations monthly in quality assurance under GOV-04 and reports any use without a valid order to the governing body at once.

responsibilities.duty: Prohibit improper restraints, obtain time-specific orders, notify representatives, track renewals and review all use.
Train staff, determine whether devices and bed rails are restraints, reassess the resident, review medications for chemical restraint and update the service plan.
Use only ordered restraints, check, reposition and offer toileting at least every 2 hours, document, and report concerns.
Issue time-specific orders that state purpose, type and duration, and renew them at least every 7 calendar days.

documentation: Physician order stating purpose, type and duration, and each 7-day renewal
Alternatives tried and the nurse's assessment
Staff training record for use of the ordered restraint
Resident and representative notification for each use
Restraint monitoring log with repositioning and toileting at least every 2 hours
Per-resident bed rail and protective device determination
Medication regimen review notes on chemical restraint
Monthly quality assurance review of restraint use

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
policies.applies_to: All staff, residents, and the Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager at all licensed levels of care (Level 1, 2 and 3)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] can protect residents before, during and after a fire, severe weather, power or water loss, infectious disease event or other emergency, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.47.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written Assisted Living Emergency Preparedness Packet that is readily available to all staff. The plan addresses what we do before, during and after an emergency, including evacuation or sheltering in place, notice to families and staff, staff coverage and assignments, and continuity of services, with supplies for at least 72 hours. The plan is reviewed at least annually. All staff are oriented to it within 24 hours of starting work. Disaster drills are held twice a year on all shifts. Programs with 50 or more residents maintain an emergency generator as required by COMAR 10.07.14.47.

definitions.definition: The written plan and supporting documents kept where all staff can reach them at any time, including on nights and weekends.
Keeping residents safely inside the building during an emergency when moving them would be more dangerous than staying.
The record of each relocated resident's name, date and time sent, alternate location, and a contact person with phone number.
A brief document that travels with each relocated resident: name, diagnosis, medications, allergies, diet, and family or legal representative contact.
A discussion-based drill that is allowed in place of a physical drill only when moving residents would be harmful.
The staff member named to coordinate with local emergency management.

procedures: The Assisted Living Manager ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) develops the Emergency Preparedness Packet and keeps a copy at [LOCATION IN BUILDING] and an electronic or off-site copy so it can be reached if the building cannot be entered. Staff on every shift must know where it is.

The Packet covers before, during and after an emergency: evacuation or shelter in place; notice to families and staff; staff coverage and assignments; and continuity of services, including food, water, medications and supplies for at least 72 hours.

The Manager names an emergency planning liaison, records the name and phone number in the Packet ([PHONE]), and gives the plan to local emergency management on request. The Manager logs the date any request is received and the date the plan is provided.

The Manager documents agreements with at least one evacuation site and with one or more transportation sources able to move residents, including residents who use wheelchairs or need stretcher or lift assistance. Agreements are kept in the Packet with a 24-hour contact for each.

The Manager sets up the resident tracking system. When any resident leaves the building in an emergency, the staff member assigned as tracker records name, date and time sent, alternate location, and a contact person with phone number.

The nurse or designee prepares a brief medical fact sheet for each resident (name, diagnosis, medications, allergies, diet, and family or legal representative contact). It is reviewed monthly, dated and kept in one central location. In an evacuation, a copy goes with each resident along with a medication supply and the resident's service plan if possible.
The Manager reviews and updates the Packet at least annually and after any actual emergency, drill finding or change in building, census or acuity. The review is signed and dated.

Within 24 hours of the start of employment, the Manager or designee orients each new employee to the plan, including routes, shelter areas, assignments and the location of the Packet. The employee signs a record that is placed in the personnel file.
On request, the Manager prepares an executive summary of the plan for residents and families and provides it within a reasonable time stated to the requester.

When an emergency occurs, the senior staff member on duty activates the plan, calls 911 if there is danger to life, and then notifies the Manager. The Manager decides on evacuation or shelter in place with emergency officials where available.
Staff notify family members or representatives and off-duty staff using the contact lists in the Packet. The Manager records who was called, when, and the response.

If a resident is relocated, staff complete the tracking record, send the fact sheet and medications, and assign a staff member or arrange for qualified personnel to continue care and medication administration at the alternate site.
Staff follow standard precautions during an emergency, including safe handling of sharps and body fluids, as in the bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan (SAF-07).
Within 24 hours of a disaster that affects residents or the building, the Manager evaluates whether a report to OHCQ is required (REC-02, SAF-02) and reports as required.

The Manager schedules disaster drills at least twice a year, covering all shifts over the year. Evacuation and shelter in place are each practiced at least once a year. A table-top exercise is used only when the Manager documents that moving residents would be harmful.

After each drill the Manager records the date, time, shift, participants, scenario, actions taken, what worked and did not, and opportunities for improvement. The Manager corrects problems and reports them to QA (GOV-04). Records are kept at least 2 years.

If [AGENCY NAME] has 50 or more residents, the Manager makes sure an emergency generator with automatic transfer is installed and tested monthly for 30 minutes with each test logged. If a waiver of this requirement is ever granted, it is disclosed to residents. Programs under 50 residents include a power-loss plan in the Packet covering refrigeration, medical equipment and heat or cooling.

responsibilities.duty: Provides funds and authority for equipment, supplies, generator (if required), and agreements needed to carry out the plan.
Develops, reviews and updates the Packet; orients staff; runs drills; maintains agreements and the tracking system; decides on evacuation; makes required reports.
Carries out the Manager's duties when the Manager is absent.
Communicates with local emergency management and provides the plan on request.
Maintains monthly-reviewed medical fact sheets and medication readiness for transport.
Know the plan and the Packet location, participate in drills, and follow assignments.

documentation: Emergency Preparedness Packet with annual review signature
Signed staff orientation record in each personnel file
Evacuation site and transportation agreements
Resident tracking records
Medical fact sheets with monthly review dates
Drill records kept 2 years
Generator test log (50+ residents)
Records of plan requests from local emergency management and of executive summaries given

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
policies.applies_to: All staff and residents; the Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager; maintenance personnel
policies.purpose: To prevent fires, make sure staff and residents can respond and evacuate safely, and meet fire safety requirements of COMAR 10.07.14.47 and .19.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] complies with local fire and building codes and NFPA 101, including Chapter 24 for one- or two-family dwellings where applicable. We keep serviced fire extinguishers in the required locations, train staff in their use at hire and annually, post floor plans with evacuation routes, hold fire drills at least quarterly on all shifts, and keep staff trained in CPR available at all times.

definitions.definition: The Life Safety Code adopted by Maryland and incorporated by COMAR 10.07.14.47.
A practice of the fire response and evacuation procedure, conducted on a scheduled shift with staff and residents.
A company licensed by the Maryland State Fire Marshal to service fire extinguishers.

procedures: Before licensure and at each renewal, the Manager obtains the fire inspection report required for the license application. In Baltimore City and Baltimore County, programs with 1-16 beds submit the health department environmental report instead. The report is kept on site.

The Manager checks that the building meets local fire and building codes and NFPA 101, including Chapter 24 where the home is a one- or two-family dwelling. Deficiencies are corrected by [DATE SET BY MANAGER] and documented.

Maintenance personnel place fire extinguishers on each floor and in or next to furnace rooms, boiler rooms, kitchens and laundries. They check monthly that each is in place, charged and unobstructed, and initial a log.
The Manager contracts with a State Fire Marshal licensee to service each extinguisher annually. Service tags and documentation are kept on site and available for surveyors.
The Manager or designee instructs each new employee in extinguisher use at hire and every employee at least annually. Attendance is recorded with signatures and kept in personnel files.
The Manager posts an individual floor plan showing evacuation routes on each floor, at eye level, and updates it whenever the layout changes.

Staff keep exits, corridors and stairways free of obstruction. If assist rails are installed in resident corridors (required on both sides at 17 or more beds), maintenance verifies they do not block egress or door swing.

The Manager schedules fire drills at least once every quarter and arranges them so that day, evening and night shifts all participate over the year. Drills are not announced to residents in a way that defeats their purpose.

During a drill, staff follow the written procedure: rescue anyone in immediate danger, activate the alarm, close doors, call 911 (in a real event), evacuate residents according to their mobility needs, and account for every resident at the assembly point using the current census.

Staff record the date and time, participants and signatures, scenario, steps taken, successful and unsuccessful actions, and opportunities for improvement. The Manager reviews the record and fixes problems promptly. Records are kept 2 years.
The Manager makes sure that at least one staff member trained in CPR is on duty 24 hours a day. The Manager reviews each shift schedule against CPR card expiration dates and records the result.

In an actual fire, the first staff member to detect it triggers the alarm, calls 911, and begins rescue and evacuation as trained. The senior staff on duty takes charge and accounts for all residents.
After any actual fire or fire department response, the Manager notifies the Alternate Manager and owner, reports to OHCQ as required (REC-02, SAF-02), and notifies families or representatives.
The Manager reviews fire safety performance, drill findings and repairs with the QA committee at least semiannually (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Schedules drills, ensures training, keeps inspection and extinguisher records, posts floor plans, and reports events.
Performs these duties when the Manager is absent.
Inspect extinguishers monthly, keep exits clear, and arrange annual servicing.
Know evacuation routes and assignments, participate in drills, maintain CPR certification where required.

documentation: Fire inspection report or health department environmental report as applicable
Extinguisher monthly check log and annual service documentation
Extinguisher training records
Fire drill records kept 2 years
CPR certification records and shift coverage review
Posted floor plans

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, volunteers and visitors; residents as applicable
policies.purpose: To reduce the risk of infection for residents and staff through training, staff health requirements, vaccination, food and laundry practices, and an exposure control plan.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] trains all staff in infection control when hired and annually. Staff must be free of communicable tuberculosis and immune to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella. The annual TB risk assessment is part of the QA plan. Flu and COVID-19 vaccines are advised for staff following CDC recommendations, and we keep records. We keep an OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan for employees with occupational exposure.

definitions.definition: Basic infection prevention practices applied to all residents, including hand hygiene, gloves, and safe handling of blood and body fluids.
Additional measures such as gloves, gowns and dedicated equipment used when a resident has an infection spread by contact.
The written OSHA plan that identifies employees at risk of exposure to blood or infectious material and describes protections.
Monitoring staff who lack evidence of immunity when disease activity in the community or facility is elevated.

procedures: Before the first day of work, the Manager or designee collects evidence that each employee is free of communicable tuberculosis and evidence of immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, and places it in the personnel file (STF-04, STF-05).

Staff who lack evidence of immunity are referred to a health care practitioner for testing or vaccination. If the staff member remains non-immune, the Manager documents surveillance when local disease activity is elevated and records any exclusions or work restrictions decided with the practitioner or health department.

Within the initial training period and at least annually, each employee receives training in infection control covering standard precautions, contact precautions and hand hygiene. The trainer, date, content and employee signature are recorded.
Each year the Manager and delegating nurse complete a TB risk assessment, document it in the QA plan, and decide whether additional screening is needed (GOV-04).

The Manager offers flu and COVID-19 vaccines according to current CDC recommendations, or provides information on where to obtain them. The record shows whether each employee received the vaccine, declined, or has a medical exemption.

Staff perform hand hygiene before and after resident contact, before medication administration and food handling, after glove removal and after using the toilet. Supplies of soap, sanitizer, gloves and paper towels are checked daily and restocked.

Staff who have vomiting, diarrhea, fever, a draining wound, or symptoms of respiratory illness report to the Manager before the shift and follow work restrictions the Manager sets, using CDC and MDH guidance.

Staff report a resident with signs of infection (fever, new cough, diarrhea, rash, wound drainage) to the nurse or Manager the same shift. The nurse assesses and notifies the practitioner (HCS-04). Contact precautions are started when indicated.

The Manager reports suspected outbreaks (two or more residents or staff with similar illness) to the local health department and OHCQ as required (REC-02) and puts in place measures such as isolation, cohorting, dining adjustments and visitor screening.

Food is kept safe: hazardous (potentially hazardous) food is held at 45°F or below, or at 140°F or above; refrigerators are at 45°F or below; freezers at 0°F or below. Staff record refrigerator and freezer temperatures daily (DL-01). Programs with 17 or more beds also meet COMAR 10.15.03 food service rules.

Laundry: staff separate soiled linens, wear gloves, do not shake soiled items, transport them in closed containers, and wash with detergent at temperatures and with disinfectants that meet manufacturer instructions and current CDC guidance (DL-03).
Housekeeping staff clean and disinfect high-touch surfaces, bathrooms and shared equipment on a written schedule using products labeled for the purpose.

The Manager adopts and updates annually a written OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan under 29 CFR 1910.1030 for employees with occupational exposure. It includes training, personal protective equipment, sharps disposal containers, and an exposure incident procedure.
After an exposure incident, the employee washes the site immediately and reports to the Manager, who arranges prompt medical evaluation and documents the incident.
Staff dispose of regulated medical waste, including sharps, in labeled puncture-resistant containers and arrange pickup through [WASTE VENDOR].
The QA committee reviews infection data, training completion and vaccination records at least semiannually (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures staff screening, training, vaccination records, outbreak reporting, and the exposure control plan.
Assesses residents with infection, advises on precautions, participates in the annual TB risk assessment, and trains staff as assigned.
Follow food safety, cleaning and laundry procedures.
Practice hand hygiene and standard precautions and report illness and exposures.

documentation: TB and immunity evidence in personnel files
Annual infection control training records
Flu and COVID-19 vaccine offer, receipt or declination records
Surveillance and work restriction records
Annual TB risk assessment in QA plan
Bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan and exposure incident records
Food and refrigeration temperature logs
Outbreak reports

policies.title: Smoking
policies.applies_to: All residents, staff, visitors and contractors
policies.purpose: To set out whether smoking is allowed at [AGENCY NAME] and to reduce fire risk and protect nonsmokers, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.48.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has a written smoking policy. Smoking at this program is [SELECT: permitted only in designated outdoor smoking areas / not permitted anywhere on the premises]. The smoking policy is provided to each resident and representative before admission and is one of the policies reviewed at survey. Where smoking is permitted, residents who smoke are assessed for help or supervision needs, and the assessment is documented in the service plan and repeated annually or after a change of condition.

definitions.definition: A specified location, set by the Manager, where smoking is allowed and where safe ash receptacles are provided.
An evaluation of a resident's ability to smoke safely, including cognition, vision, dexterity, and need for supervision or help.
Any room or area where flammable liquids, combustible gases or oxygen are used or stored.

procedures: The governing body decides whether smoking is permitted, and the Manager states the decision in this policy and in the resident agreement and admission materials.
At pre-admission, staff ask every applicant whether they smoke or vape and give the applicant and any representative a copy of the smoking policy before admission.
If smoking is not permitted, staff tell residents and visitors at admission, post signs at entrances, and offer the resident support such as contacting their practitioner about cessation options.
If smoking is permitted, the Manager designates smoking areas that comply with all local, State and federal regulations, and posts them on the floor plan and with signs.
Designated areas are equipped with ash trays of noncombustible, safe design. Staff empty them into a metal container with a lid at least daily and never into trash bins inside the building.

No smoking is allowed in any hazardous location or in any room where flammable liquids, combustible gases or oxygen are used or stored. Oxygen signs are posted on doors of rooms where oxygen is used, and smoking materials are not kept in those rooms.
Before admission, and at each admission for a resident who smokes, the delegating nurse or Manager assesses whether the resident needs help or supervision to smoke safely and records the findings.
Staff add smoking help or supervision needs, including storage of lighters and matches by staff if indicated, to the resident's service plan (ADM-04).

The nurse or Manager reassesses each resident who smokes at least annually and after any change of condition such as a fall, new medication affecting alertness, cognitive decline, or new oxygen use. The updated assessment is entered in the service plan.

When a resident on oxygen smokes or requests to smoke, the nurse reviews the risk, discusses it with the resident and practitioner, and the service plan describes the safety measures or, if the risk cannot be managed, the Manager considers whether the program can continue to serve the resident (ADM-05).

Staff who see unsafe smoking or smoking in a prohibited area stop the activity, ensure safety, and report to the Manager the same day. The Manager documents and addresses repeated violations with the resident and, if needed, the resident's representative.
Staff who smoke follow the same rules and use only designated areas away from residents during work time.
The Manager reviews smoking incidents, burns, near misses and assessment completion during QA review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether smoking is permitted and approves the policy.
Designates areas, maintains equipment and signage, enforces the policy, and ensures assessments are done on time.
Conducts or oversees smoking assessments and reassessments and updates the service plan.
Enforce the policy, supervise residents as directed in the service plan, and report violations.

documentation: Written smoking policy with approval date
Resident acknowledgment of the smoking policy at admission
Smoking assessment and annual reassessment in the service plan
Designated area map and signage
Incident reports for smoking-related events

policies.title: Visitors, Visiting Hours and Pets
policies.applies_to: Residents, visitors, representatives, volunteers and all staff
policies.purpose: To protect each resident's right to private visits and personal belongings while keeping residents safe and healthy.
policies.policy: Residents may meet or visit privately with anyone they choose. Reasonable restrictions on hours and places for visits are stated in the resident agreement and posted by the Manager. Residents may keep and use personal effects, with reasonable limits where needed for the health and safety of others. COMAR 10.07.14 contains no verified pet-specific provision, so [AGENCY NAME] sets its own pet rules covering vaccination, allergies and infection control. Visitors may be screened during outbreaks following current CDC and MDH infection control guidance.

definitions.definition: A visit in a place where the resident and visitor can talk without being overheard, such as the resident's room or a quiet common area.
A limit on hours or places that is stated in the resident agreement and posted and that serves safety, security or the rights of other residents.
An animal belonging to a resident and approved by the Manager under this policy.

procedures: The Manager sets visiting hours of [VISITING HOURS] and any restrictions on places for visits, such as areas closed during meals or housekeeping. These are written in the resident agreement (RR-04) and posted where residents and visitors can see them.
Staff explain visiting rules to residents and representatives at admission and give a copy in writing.
Staff do not prohibit or discourage any visit from a person the resident wants to see. A resident may refuse to see any visitor, and staff respect the refusal.

Staff arrange private space for visits. A resident who is on a visiting restriction ordered by a court or whose representative has legal authority is handled according to the documents on file reviewed by the Manager.
Visitors sign in at [LOCATION] with name, time in and out, and resident visited. This is for safety and emergency accounting and not to screen visitors the resident welcomes.
Visitors are not denied access outside posted hours without a safety reason. After-hours visits are accommodated when a resident is seriously ill or at end of life.

The Manager may limit or end a visit if the visitor is a danger, is impaired, or is interfering with care or others' rights. The staff member documents what happened and tells the Manager the same day. If abuse or exploitation is suspected, staff follow SAF-01.

During an outbreak or when public health officials advise, the Manager implements visitor screening or limits based on current CDC and MDH guidance, informs residents and families in advance, and allows compassionate care and end-of-life visits whenever possible (SAF-07).

Residents may retain and use their personal effects, including furniture and decorations, within room size limits and where items do not create a fire, trip, infection or safety hazard to others. The Manager explains any limit to the resident and records it.

The Manager decides whether pets are allowed. If allowed, the pet owner provides proof of current vaccinations (rabies as applicable) and a veterinarian record, and the Manager checks for resident allergies, fears and other health or safety concerns before approval.

Pets must be clean, supervised, and under the owner's or a designated person's control. The owner is responsible for feeding, litter or waste, and care. Pets stay out of food preparation areas, medication storage areas and clinical areas.

Staff who handle animal waste or pet items perform hand hygiene afterward, consistent with infection control training. Animals showing illness or aggression are removed and the Manager decides whether the pet may stay.
Visiting animals (for example therapy animals) are approved in advance by the Manager, who checks vaccination status and resident preferences.
Service animals are allowed in accordance with applicable law (RR-08).
The Manager reviews visiting concerns and pet incidents at QA (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Sets and posts visiting hours, approves pets and visiting animals, and resolves visitor disputes.
Welcome visitors, arrange privacy, maintain visitor logs, and report unsafe situations.
Care for their pets and provide vaccination records.
Advises on infection control and resident health concerns related to visitors and animals.

documentation: Resident agreement section on visiting hours and places
Posted visiting hours notice
Visitor log
Pet approval, vaccination records and owner agreement
Notes of visitor restrictions or incidents
Infection control visitor screening notices

policies.title: Physical Plant Safety: Water Temperature, Security and Common Areas
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager, maintenance and housekeeping staff, and all staff who check the physical environment
policies.purpose: To keep the building safe, accessible and comfortable by meeting Maryland standards for hot water, space, bathrooms, common areas and assist rails.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps resident hot water between 100 and 120°F at the fixture and uses anti-scald or mixing valves. We keep resident rooms, bathrooms and common space within the size and fixture standards of COMAR 10.07.14.49 through .51 and keep assist rails where required. We maintain the building securely and in good repair, consistent with applicable law and the ADA.

definitions.definition: A device that limits hot water temperature at the fixture to prevent burns.
Usable floor area of a resident room, excluding areas such as closets and bathrooms.
Common area available to residents for dining, activities and gathering.

procedures: Maintenance personnel test hot water at resident-accessible fixtures (sinks, tubs, showers) at least monthly with a calibrated thermometer, after letting the water run, and record fixture, temperature, date and initials. Acceptable temperature is 100-120°F.

If any reading is outside 100-120°F, staff stop resident use of the fixture, post a notice, tell the Manager immediately, and have the water heater or mixing valve adjusted or repaired. The fixture is retested and documented before reopening.
The Manager confirms anti-scald or mixing valves are installed and working and keeps service records. Staff check water temperature by hand before assisting a resident with bathing.

Resident rooms house no more than 2 residents. The Manager verifies each room has at least 80 square feet of functional space for a single room and 120 square feet for a double room, and records measurements in the building file.

The Manager verifies bathrooms provide at least 1 toilet and 1 sink for every 4 residents and 1 tub or shower for every 8 residents, counting residents who live in the home, and recalculates before any increase in census or bed count.
The Manager verifies at least 35 square feet of usable multipurpose common space per licensed bed and recalculates before any change in the licensed bed capacity.

If the program has 17 or more beds, the Manager confirms there are public restrooms, that food service complies with COMAR 10.15.03, and that assist rails are installed on both sides of resident corridors. Maintenance checks monthly that rails are secure, not loose and not blocked.

Housekeeping and maintenance staff perform a weekly walk-through of common areas and resident rooms looking for trip hazards, burned-out lights, damaged flooring, blocked exits, loose handrails and broken furniture. Findings are recorded and repairs scheduled with a target date.
Hazards that could cause immediate harm are blocked off and repaired the same day or the resident is moved to a safe area.

The Manager secures the building by controlling entry and exit as appropriate for resident safety and rights, with exits that can be used in an emergency. For Alzheimer's units, follow HCS-05 and SAF-03. Staff keep chemicals, tools and medications stored securely according to the policies for those items.
The Manager reviews the building for accessibility under the ADA for residents and visitors with disabilities and takes reasonable steps to remove barriers and make reasonable accommodations (RR-08).
Before opening, remodeling, or changing bed capacity, the Manager obtains required approvals from OHCQ and local authorities (GOV-02).
The Manager reports water temperature logs, repair backlog and any physical plant incidents to QA at least semiannually (GOV-04) and corrects deficiencies.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures standards are met, schedules inspections and repairs, calculates space and fixture ratios, and obtains approvals.
Test water temperatures, inspect rails and common areas, and perform repairs.
Report hazards and keep spaces clean and clear.
Report any unsafe condition and check bath water before resident use.

documentation: Water temperature log
Anti-scald valve service records
Room, bathroom and common space measurement worksheet
Assist rail inspection record (17 or more beds)
Weekly walk-through checklist and repair work orders
QA reports of physical plant findings

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
policies.applies_to: All residents; dietary, kitchen, nursing and personal care staff; Assisted Living Manager
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident receives safe, nutritionally adequate meals and snacks that meet individual needs, preferences and physician or practitioner diet orders, and that [AGENCY NAME] meets Maryland food service and food safety requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides three meals plus snacks daily. Menus are written a week ahead, posted where residents can see them, and kept for 6 months (COMAR 10.07.14.30). A licensed dietitian or nutritionist reviews the 4-week regular menu before licensure and at least every 3 years. Special and therapeutic diets are prepared or arranged as ordered and recorded in the resident record. If the licensed capacity is 17 or more beds, the kitchen follows COMAR 10.15.03 and holds a local food service permit. Smaller programs follow the basic food safety rules in COMAR 10.07.14.48 and any directive from OHCQ or the local jurisdiction. Staff who handle food receive initial and annual basic food safety training.

definitions.definition: The 4-week cycle menu served to residents who have no diet restriction.
A diet ordered by a physician or other authorized practitioner for a medical condition, such as diabetic, low sodium, renal, mechanical soft or pureed, or modified-texture diets.
Food and beverage offered between meals and at bedtime, with options that fit therapeutic diets.
A professional licensed to practice dietetics or nutrition in Maryland who reviews menus for nutritional adequacy.

procedures: The Assisted Living Manager (ALM) ensures that three meals and snacks are available every day, at times posted for residents, and that residents are told how to request food outside meal times.
Before licensure, the ALM sends the 4-week regular menu to a licensed dietitian or nutritionist for review. The reviewer's signed and dated approval is kept in the administrative file.
The ALM repeats the dietitian or nutritionist review at least every 3 years, and sooner if the menu cycle changes substantially. The ALM puts the next due date on the compliance calendar.
Dietary staff write each week's menu at least one week ahead, using the approved cycle and resident preferences. The ALM or designee reviews it.
Staff post the current week's menu in a place residents and visitors can read, in large print. Any substitution is written on the posted menu and on the file copy on the day it is made.
Staff file each posted menu, with substitutions noted, and keep it for at least 6 months. Only after that period may it be discarded.

At admission, the delegating nurse or ALM records food allergies, intolerances, cultural or religious dietary practices, chewing and swallowing problems, and preferences. This information goes into the Resident Assessment Tool and the service plan.

When a physician or other authorized practitioner orders a special or therapeutic diet, staff transcribe the order into the resident record. They update the dietary communication list in the kitchen and tell the cook the same day.

Kitchen staff prepare the ordered diet or arrange for it to be prepared. Before serving, staff check each tray or plate against the resident's diet list. Nursing or personal care staff check it again at the table.

If a resident refuses a therapeutic diet, or eats too little, staff offer an alternative that fits the order. They document the refusal and notify the delegating nurse and the practitioner as required by HCS-04.

The ALM or delegating nurse reviews diet orders at each service plan review (ADM-04) and when the resident's condition changes. Weight changes and signs of poor intake are reported to the delegating nurse.

If the licensed capacity is 17 or more beds, the ALM obtains and keeps the local food service permit and follows COMAR 10.15.03. This includes any required certified food protection manager. The permit and inspection reports are kept on site.

If the licensed capacity is under 17 beds, kitchen staff follow the basic food safety rules in COMAR 10.07.14.48 and any directive from OHCQ or the local health authority. The ALM checks the current rule text during the annual policy review (GOV-03).
Staff who prepare, handle or serve food complete basic food safety training at hire and every year. The training record goes in the personnel file (STF-05).

Staff keep food storage, refrigeration, handwashing and cleaning practices in line with these rules. Cleaning and sanitizing procedures are posted in the kitchen. No smoking is allowed in the kitchen or food preparation areas (SAF-08).
Staff make drinking water available at all times. Dietary staff keep a 3-day emergency food and water supply as required by SAF-05.
The ALM reviews resident comments about food, food-related grievances (RR-02) and menu compliance at least quarterly. Findings feed the quality assurance plan (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures meals, menus, dietitian review, permits and training are in place. Reviews menu records and food safety compliance.
Reviews diet orders, assesses nutrition and swallowing risks, and communicates diet changes to dietary staff.
Prepare and serve meals according to the menu and diet orders, follow food safety rules, and document substitutions.
Reviews the 4-week regular menu before licensure and at least every 3 years.
Verify that trays match diet lists, assist residents with eating, and report poor intake or swallowing problems.

documentation: Written menus (dated, with substitutions), kept 6 months
Dietitian or nutritionist menu review, signed and dated
Diet orders and the diet list in the resident record
Food safety training records
Local food service permit and inspection reports (17+ beds)
Resident food preferences, refusals and intake concerns

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
policies.applies_to: All residents; activities staff, direct care staff, delegating nurse and Assisted Living Manager
policies.purpose: To offer residents meaningful social, leisure, spiritual and community activities that fit their preferences and abilities, while protecting each resident's right to choose whether to take part.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides social and leisure opportunities as part of the services required by COMAR 10.07.14.30. Activities are tailored to each resident's preferences and capabilities in the service plan (COMAR 10.07.14.28A(2)). Residents may attend or decline religious services and may receive clergy visits (COMAR 10.07.14.36A(1)(m)). Participation in structured programs, including adult day care, is voluntary (COMAR 10.07.14.36D(1)). For Medicaid waiver residents, activities support community integration consistent with the HCBS settings rule at 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: A planned or spontaneous social, recreational, spiritual, educational, physical or creative event offered in the home or community.
A scheduled group program, such as a facility-run program or adult day care, that residents may choose to attend.
A resident's opportunity to take part in life outside the home, including outings, volunteering, worship and visits with friends and family.

procedures: At admission and at each reassessment, the delegating nurse or ALM interviews the resident (and the representative if one acts for the resident) about interests, hobbies, work history, faith, cultural traditions, daily routine and preferred company. The answers are recorded in the Resident Assessment Tool.

The service plan team writes the resident's activity preferences, and the support the resident needs to take part, into the service plan within 30 calendar days of admission (ADM-04). The plan is reviewed every 6 months and updated after a significant change.

The ALM or designated activities staff person writes a monthly activity calendar. It includes group, individual, physical, social, creative and spiritual activities, and options for residents who stay in their rooms or have limited mobility.
Staff post the calendar in a common area in large print and give a copy to each resident or representative on request. Changes are posted the same day.
Staff invite each resident to activities in person, never by pressure. A resident may decline any activity without penalty, and staff record the refusal without adverse comment.

Staff offer residents with cognitive impairment short, familiar, success-oriented activities that match their abilities. Staff are trained in making activities meaningful as part of cognitive impairment training (STF-03, HCS-05).
Staff provide one-to-one activities for residents who cannot or do not wish to join groups, such as conversation, music, reading, hand care or walks. Staff note them in the activity record.

The ALM arranges or helps arrange for residents to attend religious services of their choice, in the home or in the community. Clergy may visit at reasonable times, and staff protect the resident's privacy during the visit.

The ALM explains that adult day care and any other structured program are voluntary. The resident agreement discloses any adult day care policies (RR-04, RR-10). A resident is never required to attend as a condition of admission or continued stay.
Staff support residents' access to community outings, shopping, faith communities, family events and volunteer opportunities. Transportation is arranged under DL-04.
Activity staff make sure the activity supplies and spaces are safe and clean. Staff use common areas within the home's posted capacity and observe fire safety rules (SAF-06, SAF-10).
Staff document each resident's participation or refusal at least weekly in the activity record. The activity record notes any change in mood, engagement or behavior.
Staff report a sudden withdrawal, loss of interest or behavior change to the delegating nurse, who evaluates it under HCS-04 and adjusts the service plan.
The ALM asks residents for feedback on activities at least quarterly, through resident meetings or surveys, and changes the calendar as a result. Grievances are handled under RR-02.
The ALM reviews participation trends and resident feedback as part of the quality assurance plan (GOV-04) at least quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures an activity program is in place, reviews calendars and participation, and arranges community and religious access.
Plan, lead and document activities, post the calendar and invite residents without pressure.
Identifies activity needs and changes in engagement during assessments and reviews.
Help residents get to activities, offer choices, and report refusals and changes in behavior.

documentation: Monthly activity calendars
Resident activity preferences in the Resident Assessment Tool and service plan
Activity participation and refusal records
Resident feedback and meeting notes
Religious service and clergy visit arrangements

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
policies.applies_to: All housekeeping, laundry, maintenance and direct care staff; Assisted Living Manager
policies.purpose: To keep the home clean, sanitary, safe and in good repair, to provide laundry services for residents, and to comply with Maryland licensure requirements for the physical plant and with federal bloodborne pathogen rules for staff.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains the building, grounds, equipment and furnishings in clean, safe and good working order. Housekeeping and laundry services are provided as required by COMAR 10.07.14.30 and the home's other housekeeping rules. Hot water available to residents is kept between 100 and 120°F at the fixture, with anti-scald or mixing valves (COMAR 10.07.14.43). Room, bathroom and common area requirements of COMAR 10.07.14.49–.51 are maintained, including the kitchen's space to wash, sanitize and store utensils and to store garbage cans. Fire extinguishers are serviced annually by a State Fire Marshal licensee, and a generator, where required for 50 or more residents, is tested monthly. Staff handle blood and other potentially infectious materials according to 29 CFR 1910.1030.

definitions.definition: A device that limits the temperature of water delivered at a fixture to prevent burns.
Blood, certain body fluids and soiled items that may carry bloodborne pathogens.
Scheduled inspection, testing and servicing of building systems and equipment before they fail.

procedures: The ALM assigns housekeeping, laundry and maintenance duties in writing and posts a cleaning schedule. Resident rooms and bathrooms are cleaned on a regular schedule and whenever soiled.

Housekeeping staff clean and disinfect bathrooms, toilets, sinks, tubs and showers, and high-touch surfaces (door handles, rails, remote controls, call devices), using products approved for that purpose and following label directions (SAF-07).

Staff keep resident rooms, common areas and hallways clean, free of odors and clutter, and keep exits and walkways unobstructed. Common space of 35 square feet per bed and the room limits of COMAR 10.07.14.49–.51 are not reduced by storage or furniture.

Staff keep the number of residents per room, the room size, and the number of toilets, sinks and tubs/showers per resident within COMAR 10.07.14.50–.51. The ALM does not use a room or bathroom in a way that would take the home out of compliance.

Laundry staff wash bed linens at least weekly and whenever soiled, and wash towels and personal clothing on a schedule that meets resident needs. Staff label or otherwise identify each resident's clothing to prevent loss.

Staff separate soiled and clean laundry, transport soiled laundry in closed bags or containers, and do not carry it against the body. Linen contaminated with blood or body fluids is handled with gloves and, if needed, other protective equipment under 29 CFR 1910.1030.

The ALM provides gloves, gowns, face protection, red or labeled bags and sharps containers as needed. Staff receive bloodborne pathogen training at hire and every year (STF-03), and exposures are reported as in SAF-07.

Kitchen staff keep the kitchen clean. Utensils and equipment are washed, sanitized and stored in the space provided, and garbage cans are stored in the area designated for them. The kitchen is cleaned after each meal (DL-01).
Staff remove garbage daily, keep it in covered containers, and store it away from food. The ALM arranges pest control as needed and keeps service records.

The maintenance person or designee tests hot water temperature at resident-accessible fixtures at least monthly with a calibrated thermometer, and after any plumbing or water heater work. Results are logged. Water outside 100–120°F is reported to the ALM at once, the fixture is taken out of use if necessary, and the ALM has the problem fixed and rechecked the same day.

The maintenance person inspects the building at least monthly. This covers floors, walls, ceilings, lighting, heating and cooling, handrails, windows, doors, locks, call systems and outdoor walkways. Hazards are repaired promptly and written in the maintenance log.

Residents or staff report needed repairs to the maintenance person or ALM. The ALM records each request, who is fixing it and when it was fixed. Urgent hazards are dealt with immediately and the area is made safe in the meantime.

The ALM arranges annual service of fire extinguishers by a State Fire Marshal licensee, with the service tag current on every unit (SAF-06). For homes with 50 or more residents, the generator is tested monthly and the test is logged.
If a code citation is issued by a fire marshal, health or building authority, the ALM reports it to OHCQ within 7 days (REC-02) and keeps the citation and the correction record on site.
Staff move furniture, store cleaning chemicals in locked or restricted areas away from residents (when residents are at risk), and keep safety data sheets available to staff.
The ALM reviews maintenance logs, temperature logs and housekeeping complaints at least quarterly and reports trends in the quality assurance plan (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Assigns duties, ensures supplies and repairs, keeps service contracts and reports code citations to OHCQ within 7 days.
Performs inspections and repairs, tests hot water temperatures and keeps the maintenance log.
Clean rooms and common areas, launder linens and clothing, and use infection control practices.
Report hazards and repair needs, keep rooms safe, and follow bloodborne pathogen precautions.

documentation: Cleaning schedules and laundry logs
Maintenance request and repair log
Monthly hot water temperature log with corrective action
Fire extinguisher service tags and annual service records
Generator test log (50+ residents)
Pest control service records
Code citation reports and correction records
Bloodborne pathogen training records

policies.title: Transportation
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, drivers and staff who arrange or provide resident transportation
policies.purpose: To make sure residents can get to medical appointments, activities, community events and, in an emergency, to evacuation sites safely, with qualified drivers and properly insured vehicles.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides or arranges transportation for residents to activities and appointments as set out in each resident's service plan. If [AGENCY NAME] transports residents in its own or a staff or contracted vehicle, it carries the insurance required of assisted living waiver providers (COMAR 10.09.54.05). Transportation sources for emergency evacuation are covered by written agreements (COMAR 10.07.14.47). The home keeps driver qualifications and a vehicle inspection log.

definitions.definition: Transport of residents in a vehicle owned, leased or operated by [AGENCY NAME], or in a staff member's vehicle while on duty for the home.
Transport provided by another party, such as family, a public or paratransit service, a medical transport company or a Medicaid-covered non-emergency transport service.
A written agreement with a vehicle source that will carry residents if the home must be evacuated.

procedures: At assessment and service plan meetings, the delegating nurse or ALM identifies the resident's transportation needs, including medical appointments, adult day care, activities and wheelchair or other equipment needs (ADM-03, ADM-04). The resident agreement states what transportation is included and what costs extra (RR-04).
The ALM decides whether the home provides transportation itself or arranges it. The decision is recorded in the staffing and operations plan.

If the home transports residents, the ALM confirms before the first trip that automobile and liability insurance covering resident transport is in force. The ALM keeps the policy or certificate on site and renews it before it lapses.

The ALM approves each driver in writing before the driver transports residents. Approval requires a valid license for the vehicle type, a driving record review, a completed background check and exclusion check under STF-02, and orientation on this policy.
Drivers carry the license on every trip. The ALM re-verifies licensure at least annually and removes any driver whose license is suspended or revoked.

Staff inspect each home vehicle before use for tires, lights, brakes, seat belts, wheelchair securement and lift, and cleanliness. Findings go in the vehicle inspection log. A vehicle with a safety defect is taken out of service until repaired.
Staff keep vehicles maintained according to manufacturer schedules and record each service. Each vehicle carries a first aid kit and a fire extinguisher, and staff have a means of calling for help.
Staff assist residents in and out of vehicles and secure wheelchairs, walkers and oxygen. Every passenger wears a seat belt. Staff never leave a resident unattended in a vehicle.
Before each trip, the staff member confirms who is going, the time, the destination and the return time. The trip log records the resident's name, driver, vehicle, date and times.

Staff send along, when needed, the resident's medication list, face sheet, emergency contact and any appointment paperwork. If medication will be due during the trip, staff follow HCS-02 for administering or sending medications.
A staff member or a trusted person accompanies residents who have cognitive impairment, are at risk of elopement or need assistance, as the service plan states (HCS-05, SAF-03).

If an accident, injury, illness or behavior emergency happens during transport, the driver calls 911 if needed, gets the resident to safety, and notifies the ALM at once. The ALM follows SAF-02 and HCS-04 and notifies the insurer.

For emergency evacuation, the ALM keeps a written agreement with each transportation source (for example a bus company, ambulance or van service) that will carry residents. The agreements are listed in the Emergency Preparedness Packet and are reviewed at the annual plan review (SAF-05).
The ALM reviews driver files, the vehicle inspection log, insurance and evacuation transport agreements at least annually and keeps the review record on file.
The ALM cooperates with the Medicaid case manager on transportation needs for waiver residents during the case manager's quarterly visits (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Decides how transportation is provided, maintains insurance, approves drivers, and keeps evacuation transport agreements.
Hold valid licenses, inspect vehicles, transport residents safely and report accidents or problems immediately.
Identifies transportation needs and any escort or equipment needs in the assessment and service plan.
Assist residents with boarding and securement, escort residents as needed and document trips.

documentation: Insurance policy or certificate for resident transport
Driver approval, license and background and exclusion check records
Vehicle inspection and maintenance log
Trip log
Evacuation transportation agreements
Incident report for any transport accident or injury
Annual transportation review

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Staffing Plan and Supervision
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager, delegating nurse, all direct care and relief staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] has enough qualified, supervised staff on duty at all times to meet the scheduled and unscheduled needs of residents, as set out in a written staffing plan.
policies.policy: Maryland sets no numeric staff-to-resident ratio for assisted living. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a written staffing plan, based on residents' assessed needs, that covers scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day (COMAR 10.07.14.14). A staff member is present whenever a resident is in the building or is expected back. Awake overnight staff are provided whenever the Resident Assessment Tool indicates they are needed. Electronic monitoring may replace awake overnight staff only with OHCQ approval and never on an Alzheimer's special care unit (COMAR 10.07.14.14; COMAR 10.07.14.32). Dated schedules are kept on site for 18 months. Relief staff are available at all times and meet COMAR 10.07.14.19B. For Medicaid waiver homes, at least one staff member is on duty for every 8 residents in the daytime (COMAR 10.09.54.05).

definitions.definition: A written plan showing the number, type and qualifications of staff needed on each shift to meet residents' scheduled and unscheduled needs, 24 hours a day.
A staff member who is awake and on duty throughout the overnight shift.
Qualified personnel who cover absences, vacancies and unexpected needs.
The registered nurse who delegates nursing tasks to staff and supervises them under the Board of Nursing's delegation rules.

procedures: The ALM writes the staffing plan before licensure and keeps it current. For each shift it lists the number of staff, their roles and qualifications, who is on call, and how scheduled care (medications, personal care, meals, activities) and unscheduled needs (falls, illness, behaviors, emergencies, resident requests) are covered.

The ALM bases the plan on the residents' Resident Assessment Tool results, service plans and the layout of the building. The plan is reviewed at each admission, at each significant change in a resident's condition, and at least annually.
The ALM makes sure that at least one qualified staff member is physically in the building 24 hours a day whenever any resident is present or expected back. Residents are never left alone.

If the Resident Assessment Tool for any resident indicates that awake overnight staff are needed, the ALM schedules awake overnight staff for every night. The ALM records the trigger and the staffing response in the staffing plan.
On an Alzheimer's special care unit, the ALM provides awake overnight staff at all times. Electronic monitoring is never substituted on that unit (HCS-05).
If the ALM wishes to use electronic monitoring in place of awake overnight staff elsewhere, the ALM submits the request to OHCQ and does not begin the practice until OHCQ approves it in writing.

For a program that serves Medicaid waiver residents, the ALM schedules at least one staff member per 8 residents during daytime hours and checks this each week against the schedule and census (GOV-06).

The ALM writes a dated schedule for each pay period showing who works each shift, including the ALM, alternate manager and delegating nurse visits. When anyone swaps or changes a shift, the ALM changes the schedule and dates the change. Schedules are kept on site for 18 months.

The ALM keeps a list of relief personnel who are qualified under COMAR 10.07.14.19B, including background check, TB/MMR/varicella evidence, training, first aid and CPR. Relief staff are called when someone calls out and the plan cannot otherwise be met.
Each shift has at least one staff member with current first aid and CPR certification, and every staff member who gives personal care has delegating-nurse competency verification (STF-03).

A new personal care staff member who is not a CNA or GNA may work for up to 10 calendar days only while accompanied by a CNA, GNA or a person approved by the nurse, while they show competence to the delegating nurse. The ALM records the supervisor's name and the dates.
Staff who give medications are certified medication technicians working under the delegating nurse (HCS-02, HCS-03). The ALM does not schedule an uncertified person to give medications.

The delegating nurse supervises delegated tasks and observes each resident at least every 45 days as set out in HCS-03. If the ALM or delegating nurse believes staffing is not sufficient on a shift, the ALM adds staff or reduces the care load immediately.

If a scheduled staff member does not arrive, the supervisor calls relief staff, on-call staff or the alternate manager. The person leaving does not leave until relieved. The ALM writes down the gap and the response.
If on-site nursing is ordered for a resident, the ALM schedules nursing hours to match the order and records them on the schedule.
The ALM reviews staffing against incident reports, falls, call response and resident and family concerns at least quarterly and adjusts the plan (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Writes and updates the staffing plan, schedules qualified staff 24 hours a day, and keeps schedules for 18 months.
Assumes staffing and supervision duties when the ALM is absent.
Supervises delegated tasks, verifies competency and advises on staffing needs from assessments.
Confirm shift coverage, call relief staff and report gaps to the ALM.
Work assigned shifts, meet qualifications and stay until relieved.

documentation: Written staffing plan with review dates
Dated staff schedules kept 18 months
Record of Resident Assessment Tool triggers for awake overnight staff
OHCQ approval for electronic monitoring, if any
Relief staff list and qualification records
Supervision records for new non-CNA personal care staff
Records of shift coverage problems and responses

policies.title: Background Checks and Exclusion Screening
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, owners, all employees, relief staff and contractors who work in the home
policies.purpose: To protect residents by making sure no one is employed or placed in contact with residents who has a criminal history showing behavior potentially harmful to residents, or who is excluded from federal health care programs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] completes a background check on each employee within 30 calendar days before employment, and the check must show no criminal history indicating behavior potentially harmful to residents (COMAR 10.07.14.19B(2)). The criminal history records check required by Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901 is recorded in the personnel file (COMAR 10.07.14.20I). Before hire, [AGENCY NAME] checks the HHS-OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities and documents the result (COMAR 10.07.14.20O). [AGENCY NAME] does not knowingly employ anyone with a disqualifying history (COMAR 10.07.14.37B). Licensure or certification is verified with the issuing board before hire. Owners, managers and household members are also checked at licensure.

definitions.definition: A fingerprint-based check of state and national criminal history performed under Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901.

The List of Excluded Individuals/Entities kept by the HHS Office of Inspector General. Persons on it are barred under 42 USC 1320a-7 from participating in federal health care programs, including Medicaid.
A criminal history or finding indicating behavior potentially harmful to residents, such as abuse, neglect, exploitation, violence or theft.
The Maryland board that licenses or certifies a professional, such as the Board of Nursing or the Board of Long-Term Care Administrators.

procedures: The ALM tells every applicant, in writing, that employment is conditional on a satisfactory criminal history records check, an exclusion check and verification of any required license or certification.

No applicant works unsupervised or has unsupervised resident contact until the ALM has the criminal history records check result and the results of the exclusion check. The ALM does not hire until both are cleared.

The ALM or designee has each applicant complete the criminal history records check under Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901, using the process required by the State. The ALM completes the check within the 30 calendar days before the start of employment and records the date.

The ALM reviews the result to decide whether it shows criminal history indicating behavior potentially harmful to residents. The ALM records the decision, the date and the reviewer. The ALM does not knowingly employ anyone with a disqualifying history (COMAR 10.07.14.37B).

If the result is unclear or includes any matter involving abuse, neglect, exploitation, violence or theft, the ALM consults OHCQ or the owner before making an offer. The consultation is noted in the file.
Before hire, the ALM checks the name of each applicant on the HHS-OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities. The ALM prints or saves the result with the date and the checker's name and signs it.

The ALM does not hire, contract with or keep any person found on the exclusion list. If a current employee appears on the list, the ALM removes the person from all duties at once, consults the owner and notifies the Medicaid program where required.
The ALM checks the exclusion list for every current employee and contractor at least monthly. Results are recorded on a dated log with the checker's initials (GOV-05).

For a nurse, CNA, GNA, certified medication technician, delegating nurse or licensed assisted living manager, the ALM verifies the license or certificate directly with the issuing board before hire and records the number, status and expiration date (STF-03, STF-07).

The ALM calendars the expiration dates for each license and certification. A person whose license or certificate lapses stops performing the duties that require it until it is reinstated and re-verified.
The ALM also makes sure background checks are completed for owners, the ALM, the alternate manager and household members at licensure, and keeps those records with the licensing file (GOV-02).
Relief staff, agency staff and contract workers who have contact with residents go through the same checks, and the ALM obtains proof from the agency or contractor, which is kept on file.
The ALM requires every employee to report any new arrest or conviction, and any exclusion or licensure action, to the ALM within 2 business days. The ALM reviews the information under step 4.
The ALM places the criminal history records check, the review decision and the exclusion check results in the personnel file (STF-05). The file is available for OHCQ review.
Background and exclusion records are held in confidence and kept only in the personnel file, with access limited to the ALM and owner (RR-07).
The ALM audits all personnel files at least annually and keeps a record of the audit and corrections (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Completes and reviews all checks before hire, decides on eligibility, runs monthly exclusion checks and keeps records.
Supports the policy, reviews cases of concern and ensures owners and household members are checked at licensure.
