Provide accurate information, take part in the checks and report new arrests, convictions and licensure actions.
Carries out these duties when the ALM is absent.

documentation: Criminal history records check result and date
Written eligibility review decision
HHS-OIG exclusion check before hire, and monthly exclusion check log
Licensure and certification verification with the issuing board
Contractor or agency proof of checks
Employee self-report of arrests, convictions and licensure actions
Annual personnel file audit

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief (per diem) staff, the Assisted Living Manager, the Alternate Manager, medication technicians and the delegating nurse of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who works at [AGENCY NAME] is screened, oriented and trained before and during employment. Training must be suited to the needs of our residents and meet the Maryland assisted living staff qualification and training requirements, so residents are safe and the program can show a surveyor proof of training at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not allow any person to work in resident care until the hiring prerequisites in this policy are met. Each new employee receives orientation, including orientation to the emergency plan within 24 hours of starting. Training in the areas required by COMAR 10.07.14.19 is completed at hire and repeated annually where the regulation requires. Orientation and ongoing training are suited to the needs of the residents we serve (.19B(4)). Staff who administer medications are certified medication technicians. Staff who provide personal care are shown competent by the delegating nurse. Every training is documented with the proof elements required by .19F and filed in the personnel record. Relief staff meet the same requirements as regular staff.

definitions.definition: The structured introduction to the program, residents' needs, policies, the emergency plan and job duties that a new employee completes when starting work.
Employees who give hands-on help with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring and eating.
An unlicensed employee who has completed the 20-hour Maryland Board of Nursing medication technician course and holds Board of Nursing certification (.31A–B).
The registered nurse with a signed agreement with the program who delegates nursing tasks and verifies staff competency for personal care.
Per diem, float or substitute workers who fill in for regular staff. They meet the same qualifications and training requirements as regular staff.
The record that shows the date, content, completion, participant attendance, and the trainer's signature, qualifications and contact information (.19F).

procedures: Before an offer of employment becomes final, the Assisted Living Manager or HR designee confirms the applicant meets the minimum qualifications in COMAR 10.07.14.19, including age, TB screening and MMR/varicella immunity evidence (STF-04), the criminal history records check completed within 30 calendar days before employment, and the OIG exclusion list check (STF-02).
The HR designee opens the personnel file (STF-05) and a training tracking sheet for the new hire on or before the first day of work.

On the first day, and no later than 24 hours after the employee starts, the Assisted Living Manager or designee orients the employee to the emergency plan, including evacuation routes, shelter locations, the tracking system and the employee's role. The employee signs and dates the orientation record, which is filed in the personnel file.

Within the first shifts of employment, the Assisted Living Manager provides program orientation suited to resident needs. Topics include the Resident Bill of Rights, abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting (SAF-01), incident reporting (SAF-02), elopement (SAF-03), residents' service plans, dementia care where applicable, confidentiality (RR-07) and the employee's job description. New staff work alongside an experienced staff member until the manager signs off on their orientation.

Before any employee gives personal care, the delegating nurse observes the employee and confirms competency in each task the employee will perform. The nurse documents the competency and the date. Employees do not perform personal-care tasks independently until this is documented.

The HR designee verifies that each employee holds first aid training from a nationally certified instructor, and recertifies every 2 years. Licensed nurses are exempt. If an employee does not have first aid training at hire, the manager schedules it and the employee is not counted as the person trained in first aid until completed.

The Assisted Living Manager keeps a CPR coverage roster showing that at least one employee with current CPR certification that includes a hands-on component is on duty and available 24 hours a day, including nights, weekends and holidays. The manager adjusts schedules or schedules more CPR classes when a gap appears (.19D).

At hire and every year after, each employee completes training in fire and life safety (including use of fire extinguishers), infection control (SAF-07), basic food safety, and emergency and disaster plans. The manager schedules the annual cycle for each employee on the tracking sheet.

Employees complete cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training within 120 calendar days of starting: 6 hours for personal-care staff and 2 hours for other staff. Each year after, personal-care staff complete 2 hours and other staff complete 1 hour. The tracking sheet shows the 120-day due date for each new hire.

Employees who work with blood or other potentially infectious materials receive bloodborne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030 at initial assignment and annually, and are offered the hepatitis B vaccine as described in STF-04.

Before an employee administers any medication, the Assisted Living Manager verifies on the Board of Nursing certification record that the employee completed the 20-hour medication technician course and is currently certified. A copy is filed in the personnel file. Uncertified staff do not administer medications (HCS-02).

Relief staff receive the same screening, orientation, emergency plan orientation and competency validation as regular staff before their first shift. The manager does not schedule relief staff without a complete file.

For every training session, whether in-house, online or outside, the trainer or manager records the date, the content covered, a completion record, proof of each participant's attendance, and the trainer's signature, qualifications and contact information. If an outside provider issues a certificate, the manager checks that it shows these elements and adds a cover sheet if it does not.

The Assisted Living Manager reviews the training matrix monthly. Any employee whose training is overdue is told in writing, given a completion date within 14 calendar days, and removed from the related duties until the training is done.

The Assisted Living Manager adds training topics when incident reviews, grievances, quality assurance findings (GOV-04), survey deficiencies or changes in resident population show a need. These additional trainings are documented the same way.
The Administrator reviews the training program at least annually, including completion rates, and reports the results to the governing body as part of the quality assurance review.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure all hiring prerequisites and training are completed, runs orientation, maintains the CPR coverage roster and training matrix, and removes staff from duties when training is overdue.
Carries out these duties when the Assisted Living Manager is unavailable.
Validates and documents each employee's competency for personal-care tasks and supports medication technician oversight.
Opens and maintains personnel files, tracks due dates and files proof of training.
Complete required training on time, sign orientation records and provide proof of outside training.
Provides time and resources for training and reviews the program annually.

documentation: Signed emergency plan orientation record, dated within 24 hours of start
Orientation checklist signed by employee and manager
Delegating nurse competency validation for personal-care tasks
First aid and CPR certificates and the CPR coverage roster
Training records meeting the proof-of-training elements (date, content, completion, participation, trainer signature, qualifications and contact)
Cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training records with due dates
Medication technician course certificate and Board of Nursing certification verification
Bloodborne pathogens training records
Training tracking matrix and monthly review notes

policies.title: Employee Health, TB Screening and Immunizations
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, the Assisted Living Manager and the Alternate Manager of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from communicable disease and make sure staff are healthy enough to perform their assigned duties, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.
policies.policy: Before working in resident care, each employee, including the Assisted Living Manager and the Alternate Manager, gives [AGENCY NAME] evidence that they are free of communicable tuberculosis under the CDC health-care facility guidelines. Each also gives evidence of immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella by history or vaccination, and evidence that they are free of any impairment that would hinder their assigned duties (.19B(1)). Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines are advised for staff in line with CDC recommendations, and the agency documents what each employee chooses (.20K–L). When local influenza or COVID-19 activity is elevated, the agency keeps surveillance of non-immune or unvaccinated staff. Health information is kept confidential and separate from the general personnel file where practical.

definitions.definition: Testing and symptom review following CDC health-care facility guidelines to show an employee is free of communicable tuberculosis.
Documented vaccination, laboratory evidence of immunity, or a documented history of disease for measles, mumps, rubella and varicella.
A physical or mental condition that would hinder the employee from performing assigned duties safely.
Tracking which staff are non-immune or unvaccinated so exclusion or additional precautions can be applied when disease activity in the community is elevated.

procedures: The HR designee gives each applicant the employee health requirements in writing at the time of the conditional offer.

Before the first day of work in resident care, the employee provides evidence of TB screening done under the CDC health-care facility guidelines. The HR designee checks that the result is complete, dated and signed or issued by a health professional.

The employee provides documentation of immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella (vaccination records, titer results or physician-documented history). If evidence is missing, the manager arranges for the employee to obtain vaccination or testing before assignment to resident care.

The employee provides evidence from a health professional or signs a health statement affirming that they are free of any impairment that would hinder assigned duties. The manager reviews it against the job description.
The Assisted Living Manager and the Alternate Manager meet the same TB screening and MMR/varicella immunity requirements and file them in their own personnel files (.15).

If TB screening shows a positive result or symptoms, the manager refers the employee to a health care provider immediately, keeps the employee from resident care until cleared in writing, and notifies the local health department as directed by the provider or health department.

The HR designee offers influenza and COVID-19 vaccines to staff each season, advised according to CDC recommendations, and records whether each employee accepted, declined or provided proof of vaccination.
The manager keeps a confidential staff immunization list that shows, for each employee, the vaccine status for influenza and COVID-19 and immunity status for measles, mumps, rubella and varicella.

When community influenza or COVID-19 activity is elevated, as reported by the local health department or CDC, the manager reviews the list and applies infection control measures in SAF-07 to non-immune or unvaccinated staff. Those measures may include masking and exclusion from work during illness.

Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials are offered the hepatitis B vaccine at no cost, within 10 working days of initial assignment and after bloodborne pathogens training, under 29 CFR 1910.1030. Employees who decline sign a declination.
After a reported exposure to blood or body fluids, the manager arranges a confidential medical evaluation and follow-up at no cost to the employee, and documents the incident under SAF-02 and SAF-07.

Employees report to the manager if they develop symptoms of a communicable disease, including cough lasting more than 3 weeks, fever, vomiting, diarrhea or rash. The manager decides on work restrictions using SAF-07 and guidance from the local health department.

If an employee develops a condition or impairment that may hinder their assigned duties, the manager meets with the employee, asks for a health care provider's statement, and reassigns duties or arranges leave as needed.

The HR designee files all evidence of screening, immunity and vaccination status in the personnel file (STF-05) and keeps medical details beyond what the regulation requires in a separate confidential file.
The manager audits staff health records quarterly and again whenever there is a new infection control alert, and corrects any gaps within 14 calendar days.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure no employee works in resident care without required health evidence, manages exclusion and work restrictions, and maintains the immunization list and surveillance.
Collects, reviews and files health evidence and tracks vaccine offers and declinations.
Advises on infection control, TB screening results and exposure follow-up.
Provide accurate health evidence and report symptoms of illness or conditions affecting their duties.

documentation: TB screening evidence
Immunity evidence for measles, mumps, rubella and varicella
Statement of freedom from impairment that would hinder assigned duties
Influenza and COVID-19 vaccine offer, acceptance or declination records
Hepatitis B vaccine record or declination
Staff immunization and surveillance list
Exposure incident reports and follow-up records
Quarterly audit of staff health records

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, the Assisted Living Manager and the Alternate Manager of [AGENCY NAME], and the HR designee who maintains the records
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, current and organized personnel file for each staff member containing everything COMAR 10.07.14.20 requires, so compliance can be shown to a surveyor at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a separate personnel file for each employee, including the Assisted Living Manager, the Alternate Manager and relief staff. Each file contains the items required by COMAR 10.07.14.20: name, age and gender; address and phone number; education; employment history; reference notes; evaluations; attendance; emergency contact; the criminal history records check; TB and immunity documentation; influenza and COVID-19 vaccine advised records; licensure or certification; all required training and courses; and the OIG exclusion list check completed before hire. The file also contains medication technician training and certification (where applicable), the signed emergency plan orientation record, and proof of training with all required elements. Files are confidential, stored securely and available to OHCQ on request.

definitions.definition: The record, in paper or secure electronic form, that holds the required information about one employee.
A search of the federal Office of Inspector General List of Excluded Individuals and Entities before hire to confirm the person is not excluded from federal health care programs.
The check required by Maryland for employees, completed within 30 calendar days before employment as provided in STF-02.
A record of the training date, content, completion, participant attendance, and trainer's signature, qualifications and contact (.19F).

procedures: The HR designee opens a personnel file for each new hire on or before the first day of work, using the Personnel File Checklist that lists every required item.
The HR designee records identifying information: full name, age and gender, home address, phone number and an emergency contact with phone number.
The HR designee files documentation of the employee's education (diploma, transcript or signed statement with verification as available) and employment history from the application or résumé.
The HR designee documents reference checks, with the date, the person contacted and notes from each reference, before the employee starts work.

Before hire, the HR designee obtains the criminal history records check, confirms its date falls within 30 calendar days before employment, and files the result (STF-02). Results are reviewed by the Assisted Living Manager and the Administrator.
Before hire, the HR designee runs the OIG exclusion list check, prints or saves the result with the date, and files it. The employee is not hired if the check shows exclusion.
The HR designee files TB screening evidence and evidence of immunity for measles, mumps, rubella and varicella (STF-04) and records the influenza and COVID-19 vaccine offered, accepted or declined.

The HR designee files copies of professional licenses and certifications, such as nursing licenses, nurse aide certification and first aid and CPR cards, and records expiration dates on the tracking sheet.
For medication technicians, the HR designee files the Board of Nursing course completion and certification, and records the certification renewal date.
The HR designee files the signed and dated emergency plan orientation record showing orientation within 24 hours of starting work.

The HR designee files every training record for orientation and annual training and confirms each shows the date, content, completion record, participation proof, and trainer's signature, qualifications and contact information.
The Assisted Living Manager completes and files written performance evaluations and records attendance, and the manager reviews the evaluations with the employee.

The HR designee audits each file against the checklist within 30 calendar days of hire and again every 6 months. The manager corrects any missing item within 14 calendar days and documents the correction.

Files are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator, the Assisted Living Manager, the Alternate Manager and the HR designee may open them, plus OHCQ and other authorized surveyors.
The Assisted Living Manager makes personnel files available to OHCQ surveyors during surveys and complaint investigations. The manager does not alter, backdate or remove any item.
After an employee leaves, the file is kept, secured and retained as the retention schedule adopted by [AGENCY NAME] requires, and is not discarded before that schedule allows.

responsibilities.duty: Creates and maintains personnel files, uses the checklist, tracks expirations and conducts file audits.
Reviews background and exclusion results, completes evaluations, makes sure files are complete and corrects gaps.
Approves hires only when the file is complete and oversees confidentiality and secure storage.
Provide accurate documents, copies of renewals and proof of outside training.

documentation: Personnel File Checklist for each employee
Identification, address, emergency contact and education records
Employment history, reference notes, evaluations and attendance
Criminal history records check and OIG exclusion check with dates
TB, immunity and vaccine records
Licenses, certifications and expiration tracking sheet
Medication technician training and certification
Signed emergency plan orientation record
Proof-of-training records
File audit records

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, volunteers, contractors, the Assisted Living Manager, the Alternate Manager and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To set expectations for how staff treat residents, protect residents' dignity, privacy and finances, and maintain professional boundaries, in line with Maryland's residents' rights and abuse, neglect and exploitation requirements.
policies.policy: Every person working at [AGENCY NAME] treats residents with consideration, respect and dignity (.36A(1)(a)). Staff knock before entering a resident's room (.36A(1)(g)) and protect resident confidentiality (.36B). Residents are not assigned work without their consent and appropriate compensation (.36C). Staff who witness or suspect abuse, neglect or financial exploitation report it within 24 hours as required by COMAR 10.07.14.37 and SAF-01, and licensed or certified staff who do not report may be referred to their licensing or certifying board (.37C). Staff training includes residents' rights (.19B(7)(d)). The manager's obligations under .37 and the related resident-funds requirements apply to any financial dealing with residents, and a licensee who commits financial exploitation violates the chapter and applicable civil and criminal laws. Rules on gifts, loans and personal financial dealings with residents in this policy are [AGENCY NAME]'s own operator rules and are not requirements of a specific COMAR section.

definitions.definition: The limit between a staff member's professional role and a personal, financial or intimate relationship with a resident.
Improper use of a resident's money, property or resources for the benefit of someone other than the resident.
Money, goods, services or favors of any value given to a staff member by a resident, a resident's family or representative.
Any adverse action against a resident or staff member because of a complaint or report.

procedures: At hire, each employee receives and signs the Staff Code of Conduct and this policy. The signed copies are filed in the personnel file (STF-05).
Each employee completes training on the Resident Bill of Rights during orientation and annually, and the training record is filed (STF-03).

Staff address residents by their preferred name, speak respectfully, maintain privacy during care and offer choices in daily routines. Staff do not shout at, demean, mock, threaten or ignore residents.
Staff knock and wait for a response before entering a resident's room, and then identify themselves, except in an emergency. Staff close doors and curtains during personal care.

Staff discuss resident information only with those who need it for care or who are authorized under RR-07. Staff do not discuss residents in public areas or on social media and do not photograph or record residents without written consent.
Staff do not ask residents to perform work for the facility. Any work a resident chooses to do is voluntary, consented to in writing and appropriately compensated (RR-10).

Staff do not accept gifts of cash or any gift above a nominal value from residents or families. Staff do not borrow or lend money or property to or from residents, become named on residents' wills, accounts or powers of attorney, or accept loans. A staff member offered such an item tells the manager the same day, and the manager records it. This is an operator rule of [AGENCY NAME].
Staff do not handle a resident's money, bank cards, checks or valuables except through the resident funds procedure in RR-05, with receipts and two-person verification where required.
Staff do not sell products or services to residents, do not use residents' property for personal use and do not have romantic or sexual relationships with residents.
Staff keep contact with residents and families outside work limited. They do not give personal phone numbers or social media contacts to residents, except as the manager approves for resident care.

Any staff member who sees, hears of or suspects abuse, neglect or financial exploitation immediately protects the resident, tells the manager and reports within 24 hours as described in SAF-01 to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, the local Department of Human Services/APS and the manager. Staff may report directly, and no one needs a supervisor's permission.
Licensed or certified staff are told at orientation that failure to report may be referred to their board (.37C).
The manager protects any person who reports from retaliation. Any retaliation is itself a violation of this policy and leads to discipline up to termination.

The manager investigates every report of a conduct violation promptly, interviews witnesses, documents findings and applies progressive discipline, including termination and report to the licensing board when required.
The manager reviews conduct concerns, grievances (RR-02) and incident trends quarterly and plans additional training as needed (GOV-04).
Staff who are unsure whether a situation crosses a boundary ask the Assisted Living Manager or Administrator before acting.

responsibilities.duty: Follow the code of conduct, protect residents' rights and dignity, and report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation within 24 hours.
Trains staff, supervises conduct, investigates concerns and ensures no retaliation.
Enforces discipline, reports to boards when required and oversees the code of conduct annually.
Files signed code of conduct acknowledgments and training records.

policies.title: Assisted Living Manager Licensure, Training and Continuing Education
policies.applies_to: The Assisted Living Manager, the Alternate Manager, the Administrator and the governing body of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is always managed by an Assisted Living Manager who meets Maryland's licensure, training, background and health requirements, and that a qualified Alternate Manager is available when the manager is not.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs an Assisted Living Manager who is at least 21 years old, holds a high school diploma and meets the requirements of COMAR 10.07.14.15, including any added education and experience requirements for Level 3. From July 1, 2026, the manager must hold an assisted living manager license from the Maryland State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators (Health Occupations §9-3A-01). The manager completes the OHCQ-approved 80-hour course with exam (HG §19-1807) and then 20 hours of continuing education every 2 years. The manager has a current criminal background check, TB screening, MMR and varicella immunity, and first aid and CPR. A provisional period is up to 90 days, extendable up to 30 days, as provided in Health Occupations §9-3A-01(b)(2). The Alternate Manager is 21 or older, has 2 years of health-related experience, meets the staff qualifications in .19B(1)–(7) and takes over when the manager is unavailable. Failure to meet the training requirement carries a penalty of up to $10,000.

definitions.definition: The individual responsible for the day-to-day operation of the program and who holds the qualifications and license required by Maryland.
A qualified person designated to act as manager when the Assisted Living Manager is unavailable (.18).
The OHCQ-approved assisted living manager training course with exam.
20 hours of training that the manager completes every 2 years after the initial course.
A temporary period of up to 90 days, extendable by up to 30 days, under Health Occupations §9-3A-01(b)(2) as enacted by SB 613.
The Maryland State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators.

procedures: Before hiring or designating an Assisted Living Manager, the Administrator verifies the candidate is at least 21 years old, holds a high school diploma and meets any added Level 3 education and experience requirements if the program is licensed at Level 3.

The Administrator verifies the candidate's current Board of Long-Term Care Administrators assisted living manager license on the Board's public verification page for any start date on or after July 1, 2026, and files a printed verification in the manager's personnel file.
The Administrator confirms the candidate's completion of the OHCQ-approved 80-hour course and exam by obtaining the certificate from the approved training vendor and filing a copy.

The manager candidate completes the State and FBI criminal history records check required by the Board and the agency's background check under STF-02, and provides current TB screening and MMR and varicella immunity (STF-04) and first aid and CPR certificates. The Administrator reviews all results before the manager starts.

If the Board issues a provisional status, the Administrator records the start and end dates, calendars the end date and a 30-day reminder, and tracks what the manager must complete before the period ends. The agency does not assume an extension of up to 30 days will be granted.
Where a person is acting under a provisional period, the Administrator keeps the Board's written notice on file and ensures that person meets all other qualification requirements.
The Assisted Living Manager keeps the Board license verification posted with the facility license so residents, families and surveyors can see it, and replaces it when the license is renewed.
The manager tracks the 2-year continuing education cycle: 20 hours of CE every 2 years. The manager records dates, topics, hours and provider on a CE log and files certificates in the personnel file.
The Administrator checks the CE log every 6 months. If the manager is not on track, the Administrator schedules courses so the 20 hours are completed at least 60 calendar days before the cycle ends.
The manager renews the Board license as the Board requires and gives the Administrator proof of renewal before expiration. The manager does not work with an expired license.

The Administrator designates an Alternate Manager in writing. Before designation, the Administrator verifies age 21 or older, at least 2 years of health-related experience, and the staff qualifications in .19B(1)–(7) incorporated by .18, and files this proof in the Alternate Manager's personnel file.

The Assisted Living Manager informs the Alternate Manager and all staff of each planned absence and the dates when the Alternate Manager is in charge. Staff schedules, the call list and the posted emergency contacts show who is the manager or alternate in charge at all times.

The Alternate Manager has authority to act on all manager duties during an absence, including staffing, incident response, resident safety decisions and contact with OHCQ, and reports to the manager and Administrator on return.

If the manager leaves or can no longer serve, the Administrator promptly places the Alternate Manager in charge, begins recruitment of a licensed replacement and notifies OHCQ of the change as required by REC-02.
The Administrator reports the status of the manager and Alternate Manager licensure, training and CE to the governing body at least annually (GOV-01).
The Administrator keeps current contact information for the Board, (410) 767-6500, and OHCQ, (410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005, in the manager's file and the administrative office.

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff of [AGENCY NAME] who create, use, store, release or dispose of resident records, including the Assisted Living Manager, the delegating nurse and medication technicians
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident has a complete, accurate, secure and confidential record that supports care, can be reviewed by the resident and surveyors as permitted, and is kept for the time required by Maryland.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a secure, confidential individual record for each resident at the program (COMAR 10.07.14.29A). The record includes Resident Assessment Tools, nursing assessments, medical orders, service plans, care notes, an emergency data sheet, advance directives, MOLST, monthly weights, pharmacy reviews and rehabilitation plans. Care notes are individualized, legible, dated, timed and signed. Records are kept for 5 years after discharge. Records are released and disposed of as the Maryland Confidentiality of Medical Records Act (Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3) permits. Resident confidentiality is a resident right (COMAR 10.07.14.36). Resident records support the service plan required by COMAR 10.07.14.28.

definitions.definition: The individual record that contains the information required by COMAR 10.07.14.29A for one resident.
A dated, timed and signed entry that describes the resident's condition, care provided or events, written in individualized terms.
Maryland Medical Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment, kept in the record (RR-06).
A summary sheet of identifying, medical, medication and contact information that travels with the resident in an emergency.
The 5 years after discharge during which the agency must keep the resident's record.

procedures: On or before the day of admission, the Assisted Living Manager opens a record for the resident using the standard record format, with a labeled section for each required content item.

The record includes: Resident Assessment Tools; nursing assessments; medical orders; service plans; care notes; the emergency data sheet; advance directives; MOLST; monthly weights; pharmacy reviews; and rehabilitation plans. The manager reviews each record for completeness at admission and monthly.

The delegating nurse files the Resident Assessment Tool and nursing assessment on admission and on each reassessment, and the service plan is developed from these within 30 calendar days of admission. The nurse reassesses within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization and at least annually, files each assessment, and reviews the service plan every 6 months (ADM-03, ADM-04).
On readmission after a hospital stay, the delegating nurse reassesses the resident within 48 hours and files the reassessment in the record.

Staff write care notes on admission, at least weekly, on significant changes and incidents, on transfer, on return from appointments or nonroutine leaves, when the resident is seen by a practitioner, and at discharge.

Each care note is individualized to the resident, legible, dated, timed and signed with the writer's full name and title. Staff do not use white-out, erase or backdate. Errors are corrected with a single line through the entry, the date, the writer's initials and the correct entry.

The manager reviews a sample of care notes each month to confirm weekly notes are being written, entries follow events and each note is signed and timed. Findings go to the quality assurance review (GOV-04).
Staff file monthly resident weights in the record by the 5th day of the next month, and the nurse reviews weight changes with the practitioner when needed (HCS-04).
The manager files pharmacy reviews, advance directives, MOLST and rehabilitation plans when received, and updates the emergency data sheet at every significant change and at least every 6 months.

Active records are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system, and only staff who need the information for the resident's care or for administration may access it. Staff do not leave records open or unattended in common areas (RR-07).

The manager releases information from a resident's record only as Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3 and the facility's RR-07 policy permit. This includes the resident, an authorized resident representative, treating practitioners, and OHCQ surveyors. The manager logs each release with date, recipient, purpose and what was released.
A resident or authorized representative may ask to see the resident's record. The manager arranges review within a reasonable time with a staff member present and records the request and date.

After a resident is discharged or dies, the manager completes the record within 7 calendar days, including the discharge or death note, and moves it to closed storage. The record is retained for 5 years after discharge. A label shows the discharge date and the earliest destruction date.

If [AGENCY NAME] plans to close, the Administrator arranges in writing for the retention and secure storage of all resident records for the full retention period and tells OHCQ and residents or representatives where the records will be kept.
On a change of ownership, the prior owner gives the records of current residents to the new owner before the new license is issued, and the Administrator keeps a transfer list.

After the retention period, the manager has records destroyed by shredding or secure electronic deletion in a manner consistent with Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3, and records the date, method and records destroyed. Records involved in a pending survey, complaint or legal matter are not destroyed.

The Administrator keeps related records for their own periods: staffing schedules for 18 months, fire and disaster drill records for 2 years and menus for 6 months. [AGENCY NAME] also keeps privacy policies and related HIPAA administrative documentation for at least 6 years, consistent with 45 CFR 164.530.

Completes and files nursing assessments, reassessments and service plan reviews on time.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: All staff, the Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager, the Delegating Nurse, the Governing Body and the owner(s) of [AGENCY NAME], at all levels of care (Level 1, 2 and 3) and in any Alzheimer's special care unit.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] reports every required event, change and document to the Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) and to the other agencies named in COMAR 10.07.14 on time, in writing, and with a record that the report was made.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will make every report required of a licensed assisted living program to OHCQ, law enforcement, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services (APS), the Division of Drug Control and local emergency management, within the deadline set by regulation. Suspected abuse, neglect or financial exploitation will be reported within 24 hours (C35). Incident reports will be completed within 24 hours of knowledge (C31). Certain resident deaths will be reported to OHCQ within 24 hours (C31). Changes that affect the license will be reported to OHCQ as required, and prior OHCQ approval will be obtained before beds or the level of care are increased or an Alzheimer's special care unit is operated (C8, C30). No staff member may delay or avoid a required report to protect the program, a co-worker or a resident's family. No one will be penalized for making a report in good faith. The Assisted Living Manager is responsible for these reports. The Alternate Manager or the person in charge makes them whenever the Manager is unavailable, so no deadline is missed. The Governing Body is responsible for license-level changes. A missed or late report is itself an incident, will be reviewed under the Quality Assurance Plan, and may carry a monetary penalty (up to $1,000 where abuse, neglect or exploitation is not reported within 3 days) (C35).

definitions.definition: The Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality, Assisted Living Team, which licenses and surveys assisted living programs. Phone (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005; fax (410) 402-8211.
The moment any staff member sees, is told of, or reasonably suspects a reportable event. The 24-hour clock starts then, not when the Manager is told.

definitions.term: Reportable abuse, neglect or financial exploitation
definitions.definition: Any suspected or alleged abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a resident, whoever the alleged actor is (staff, other resident, family, visitor or other person), as described in policy SAF-01.

A written record of an accident, injury, death, elopement, medication error or other significant event involving a resident, completed on the program's incident report form within 24 hours of knowledge (C31).
The written response [AGENCY NAME] sends to OHCQ after a survey or inspection that cites deficiencies, describing how and when each will be corrected.
The standard written statement of the services, fees and policies of the program, given to prospective residents and kept current as described in policy GOV-02.

procedures: Required-report calendar: The Assisted Living Manager keeps a Required Reports Matrix (Attachment A to this policy) at the manager's office and the nurses' station. It lists each report, the recipient, the deadline, the form and who makes it. The Manager reviews and updates the Matrix at least annually, and whenever regulations or the license change, under policy GOV-03.

Suspected abuse, neglect or financial exploitation (24-hour report): Any staff member who sees or suspects it first ensures the resident's immediate safety, then tells the Manager or person in charge at once. The report must not wait for the Manager's investigation or for proof.

Within 24 hours of knowledge, the Manager (or the Alternate Manager or person in charge) reports by phone, followed by the written report, to all of the following: (a) law enforcement, as appropriate; (b) OHCQ at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005; (c) the local Ombudsman or area agency on aging at [LOCAL OMBUDSMAN PHONE]; (d) the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services at [LOCAL DHS/APS PHONE]; and (e) the Assisted Living Manager, if the person reporting is not the Manager (C35). If an emergency exists, staff call 911 first.

The Manager does not alter, shorten or hold back a report because of a disagreement with the report. Any staff member may make the report directly if the Manager is unavailable or declines. The report is not delayed past 3 days under any circumstances, because late reporting can carry a penalty of up to $1,000 (C35).

Investigation and follow-up report: The Manager starts an on-site investigation immediately, keeps all investigation records on site, and sends the written investigation report to the same agencies that received the initial report (C35). Details are in policy SAF-01. The Manager records on the Report Log the date, time, agency, person spoken to and method for each report.

Incident reports (24 hours): The staff member who knows of an incident completes the incident report form in full, and in any case within 24 hours of knowledge (C31). The Manager reviews it the same day, completes any required notifications (resident representative, practitioner, others) and files the report. Incident reports are kept on the premises and made available to OHCQ on request (C31). See policy SAF-02.

Resident deaths: When a resident dies as a result of abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, a medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program, the Manager notifies OHCQ within 24 hours of the death (C31) by phone at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005, and also completes an incident report and any report required under policy SAF-01. If the cause is unknown or unclear, the Manager treats it as potentially reportable and consults OHCQ the same day. See HCS-09.

Changes to the license application: The Governing Body or Manager notifies OHCQ immediately of any change to the information in the license application (for example the owner, Manager, address, telephone or contact information) (C8). Written notice goes to OHCQ the same day it is known, and a copy is placed in the license file.

Code citations: The Manager reports any code citation (for example from the fire marshal, health department or building inspector) to OHCQ within 7 days (C8) and keeps a copy of the citation and the report in the license file.

Bed increases and level-of-care increases: [AGENCY NAME] does not add beds and does not raise the licensed level of care (Level 1, 2 or 3) until OHCQ has given written approval (C8). The Governing Body files the request, tracks it to approval and does not admit residents to the new beds or at the new level before approval.

Ownership change, relocation or closure: For a program with 49 or fewer beds, the Governing Body gives OHCQ at least 60 days' notice before a change of ownership, a relocation or a closure (C8). The Governing Body keeps the proof of mailing or delivery. For a closure or relocation, the Manager also follows policy ADM-06 so that residents and representatives receive their own required notices and help with relocation.

Good standing: The Governing Body confirms with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) that the entity remains in good standing, files the annual report on time, and informs OHCQ of any change in status, since good standing is a condition of the license (C8). See GOV-02.

Alzheimer's special care unit: Before the program operates or advertises a special care unit, the Governing Body submits the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form to OHCQ and obtains OHCQ's written approval (C30). The Manager keeps the approval on file. The unit has awake overnight staff as required (C30); any change that affects the disclosed information is reported to OHCQ before it takes effect. See HCS-05.

Uniform Disclosure Statement: When a service, fee or policy change affects the contents of the UDS, the Manager amends the UDS and gives the amended version to OHCQ within 30 days of the change, then gives it to residents and representatives as described in GOV-02 and RR-04.

Delegating nurse changes: The Manager keeps the signed RN agreement and Board of Nursing delegating nurse course proof on file and ensures the nurse is on site to observe each resident at least every 45 days and on call at all times (C19). Because the prior version of the rule required notice to OHCQ when a delegating nurse relationship ends, before finalizing this policy the Manager must confirm the current notice requirement in COMAR 10.07.14.21 (C19) or with OHCQ. As a [AGENCY NAME] standard, whenever the delegating nurse changes or leaves, the Manager informs OHCQ in writing by the next business day, names the replacement nurse, and has the replacement's signed agreement in place before any further delegation. Nursing coverage does not lapse. See HCS-03.

Controlled substance destruction: Within 10 calendar days of destroying controlled substances, the Manager (or delegating nurse) sends the destruction form to the Division of Drug Control and keeps a copy in the medication disposal record. See HCS-01.

Plan of correction: When OHCQ cites deficiencies, the Manager sends the signed plan of correction to OHCQ within 10 business days of receiving the statement of deficiencies. The plan says what will be done, who is responsible and the correction date for each deficiency. The Manager tracks completion, keeps evidence of correction, and reports results to the Governing Body and under GOV-04.
Emergency plan: When local emergency management asks for the program's emergency plan, the Manager provides the current plan promptly and records the date and recipient. See SAF-05.

Surveyor and records requests: When OHCQ asks for incident reports, investigation records, training proof (C17), delegating nurse documents (C19) or other records, the Manager provides them promptly. Incident reports must be available on the premises (C31). Resident records are kept as required in REC-01.

Monthly audit: Each month the Manager reviews the Report Log, incident reports, resident deaths and pending requests to OHCQ to confirm every required report was made on time and every approval was received. Late or missed reports are corrected immediately, the cause is recorded, and the findings are reported to the Governing Body and used under GOV-04.

Makes or directs all 24-hour, 7-day and 10-day reports, keeps the Required Reports Matrix and Report Log, files plans of correction, amends the UDS, and conducts the monthly audit.
